notes.title: 20XX 0.959b Patch Notes -- August 17, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's patch adds new Frostor level pieces (part 1 of 2), a new way to spend Soul Chips in the Ark, and generally fixes a bunch of stuff up. (It's a smaller patch on account of me being out of town for a week of it.)

NB: We're going to be at PAX Prime (West?) in two short weeks - if you're going to be there, come find us in the Indie MEGABOOTH and say hi! (Also, on the off chance that anyone wants to help us man the booth from time to time, we won't turn down good help!)

Also NB: We skipped the SF patch this cycle around, but there should be one next week.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note, seriously, this time: 20XX's price will increase to the final price of $15 in conjunction with 20XX's next patch on August 31. This is not a statement that we're about to go to full release or launch Level 9; 20XX has come a long way since the price went up to $12. There's still lots of work to do on Level 9, and a ton of other stuff to get done before 1.0!

TL;DR for today's patch: Frostor pieces! (Get ready for more weirdly placed Frostor things!) Token Machine! Game Over screen! Pre-boss stuff! Crash fixes!

For the next few patches: More Frostor pieces & hopefully Jungle pieces part 1! Narrative!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

New Frostor level pieces (part 1 of 2).
Frostor Bombhive tweaks:

Now fizzles out if the player gets far away enough, allowing players to run past properly.
HP reduced by 40%.
Latch on -> explode timer increased by 33%.
No longer grants points in Challenges (to make them more optional to kill).

The Token Machine has been added to the Ark. Spend your excess Soul Chips on Tokens for your next run! You can buy however many you have Chips for.

The price increases for each Token purchased, but resets whenever the player returns to the Ark from a run.

Revamped the Game Over screen!
Revamped level-end and pre-boss rewards a bit - instead of a locked Shop teleporter always showing up before a boss and a random Machine spawning afterwards, the pre-boss hallway now *may* contain a free crate, usually contains a Machine of some kind, and sometimes contains a Shop teleporter (unlocked, no $$ needed).

This pre-boss Machine can be the special new Cheap Health Machine, which only costs 2 nuts per use.



SMALL CHANGES:

Splinterfrost can now be fired straight ahead or at 45 degree angles from straight (diagonals forward/up and forward/down).
Slight performance improvements.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed another cause of the "invisible & stationary enemy" bug.
Fixed a crash relating to hitting bosses with their weaknesses while Damage Numbers were turned off.
Fixed an issue causing some folks with unusual hardware from being able to start the game (hopefully - this should be the d3dcDevice failure issue - if you still see this, please report)! These players may still experience issues trying to switch to fullscreen after the game is up - tell us what happens! 

This fix temporarily disables those users from being able to start the game in "true" fullscreen, but at least it'll run. More coming!



KNOWN ISSUES:

Machines still display in odd places sometimes in online co-op -- really looking to fix this one for next patch!


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.958 Patch Notes -- August 3, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch gives its Powers some much-needed love in the form of level interactions! Every Power now does something non-combat related. Additionally, we've added some new Options, and done some much needed renderer reworking that should improve performance for folks playing 20XX on potato-based systems. (It should also improve performance for folks playing 20XX on computers.) This patch also reworks Frostor's "targeter" mechanic, replacing it with the deadly Bombhive. Enjoy!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!
We're planning on mucking around with the game's options/save data over the next patch or two, so this is a pretty real possibility.

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

NB: I'm going to be out of town without much internet access until August 6th, so I won't be super available on the forums/by email.

TL;DR for today's patch: Power interactions! Options! Renderer rewrite! Targeter rework!

For the next few patches: Boss iterations! Narrative!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Rewrote a section of 20XX's renderer from scratch. Performance should be improved (maybe even greatly!) on most systems.
Power interactions! Each Power now has a unique property, most of which interact with the level environment. Discover them all! (Hint: The Quint Laser has two.)
Lots of Options changes:

Display Modes: 20XX finally adds "Fullscreen (v-sync)" and "Fullscreen (no v-sync)" to its list of Display Modes. They even display in the resolution you actually select!
20XX now remembers what character the first player previously used on startup. Ace players rejoice!
20XX now remembers the last thing you set "Display Run Time" to.
There's now a "Restore Defaults" button.
Added a "Hide Numbers" option. It'll hide damage numbers.
Added a "Health Display Type" option. Hybrid (default) shows bars until health or energy exceeds 20, at which point it switches to numeric. Bars or Numbers can be permanently turned on as well.



SMALL CHANGES:

Looping sounds no longer persist while the game is paused.
Tightened up the end-level bonus chest award effect.


BUG FIXES:

Hopefully fixed the "phantom enemy" bug.
Fixed an issue causing a bonus area to spawn right over the boss hallway, resulting in it being blocked by the boss barrier.


KNOWN ISSUES:

Some users may experience stuttering in Borderless Windowed mode - if this is you, please report it!
The patch number and up


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.957b Patch Notes -- July 20, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch fixes up our new Vile Visage, introduces some changes to the way levels are generated, and much more!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

We're planning on mucking around with the game's options/save data over the next patch or two, so this is a pretty real possibility.

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

NB: I'm going to be out of town without much internet access from July 30th to August 6th, so I won't be super available on the forums/by email. The August 3rd patch will still proceed as scheduled.

TL;DR for today's patch: VV polish (round 1) - level gen changes - menu changes - Defiant Mode - plenty of fixes!

For the next few patches: Frostor targeter changes (seriously next patch this time!), a little more end of level feel, Power->Level interactions (yes, you read right! Powers will do stuff in level environments), Options, Narrative!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Some changes to the way earlygame levels are generated:

Level 1 is now somewhat longer.
Level 2 is now slightly shorter. (Same length as the new level 1.)
Level 7 is now somewhat longer. (Somewhat longer than 6, slightly shorter than 8.)
In all Challenge modes, levels are no longer generated as "level 1" - the game treats level 1 as level 2 for purposes of difficulty. (The first level of a High Tide Challenge run is still difficulty 5, not 6.)

Note to our Community readers and posters - this set of changes is the result of a long Community thread about level length from some time ago. The thread explored ways to keep the game interesting for veteran players and included a discussion on end-of-level rewards and the bonus timer - this is the result of that discussion. We aren't comfortable with adding sharp scoring metrics to each level of normal play based on damage taken, enemies slain, etc, since those are already incentivized by the game's rules. Instead, we've eliminated "level 1" from Challenges entirely -- the game treats any "level 1" as "level 2" for purposes of difficulty -- and smoothed out the level length gap between level 1 and 2 (by making 1 some longer and 2 some shorter).


Lots of fight tweaks to our new Vile Visage! (More are actually coming next patch.)
Repositioned the end of level and bonus timer chests, and gave them some new effects.


SMALL CHANGES:

When exiting an air dash, players now enter the "dash jump" state instead of the "jump" state if the player is still holding down Dash.
Hardcore Challenge teleporters in the hub now first pop up some details on the Skulls involved.
The "Skulls" object in the hub has been replaced with the "Defiant" game mode.

The functionality is effectively identical -- instead of turning on Skulls then starting a Normal game, you just choose the Skulls in Defiant Mode and play there.
Toggling Skulls previously only affected Normal anyway, so this seemed a little more straightforward.
When playing with Skulls on in Defiant Mode, Soul Chip yield is increased (by fidgety numbers we're not sharing publicly yet because they'll probably change).

Marathon and Endless do not give increased SC yields. High Tide counts as 2 Skulls for determining SC yield, and Rock counts as 3.


Eternal Star's Level 8 batbros are now 20% likely to spawn as exploders (down from 100%). They'll also be colored differently.
Adjusted Eternal Star's boss room. It's a little more navigable, and Player 2's HUD won't block the bottom left corner anymore.
The Purist skull now also disables Core Augs. (Core chests are replaced by normal Aug chests.)
Changed the "Soul Foe" glow (pretty drastically) so they no longer appear almost invisible against certain backgrounds.
Two new Augs!
Some Menu changes (mostly cosmetic, for now -- the big Options Patch is probably next patch).
Volume settings now adjust as you scroll, instead of on hitting Confirm.
The end-of-level barrier is now much taller.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed Ace's Glaive not caring about boss invuln while in midair.
Fixed the co-op Power re-map bug.
(hopefully) Fixed a bug causing the occasional invisible enemy. (I think it was introduced in the same patch that added the various room teleporters.)

notes.title: 20XX 0.957b Patch Notes -- July 20, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch fixes up our new Vile Visage, introduces some changes to the way levels are generated, and much more!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

We're planning on mucking around with the game's options/save data over the next patch or two, so this is a pretty real possibility.

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

NB: I'm going to be out of town without much internet access from July 30th to August 6th, so I won't be super available on the forums/by email. The August 3rd patch will still proceed as scheduled.

TL;DR for today's patch: VV polish (round 1) - level gen changes - menu changes - Defiant Mode - plenty of fixes!

For the next few patches: Frostor targeter changes (seriously next patch this time!), a little more end of level feel, Power->Level interactions (yes, you read right! Powers will do stuff in level environments), Options, Narrative!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Some changes to the way earlygame levels are generated:

Level 1 is now somewhat longer.
Level 2 is now slightly shorter. (Same length as the new level 1.)
Level 7 is now somewhat longer. (Somewhat longer than 6, slightly shorter than 8.)
In all Challenge modes, levels are no longer generated as "level 1" - the game treats level 1 as level 2 for purposes of difficulty. (The first level of a High Tide Challenge run is still difficulty 5, not 6.)

Note to our Community readers and posters - this set of changes is the result of a long Community thread about level length from some time ago. The thread explored ways to keep the game interesting for veteran players and included a discussion on end-of-level rewards and the bonus timer - this is the result of that discussion. We aren't comfortable with adding sharp scoring metrics to each level of normal play based on damage taken, enemies slain, etc, since those are already incentivized by the game's rules. Instead, we've eliminated "level 1" from Challenges entirely -- the game treats any "level 1" as "level 2" for purposes of difficulty -- and smoothed out the level length gap between level 1 and 2 (by making 1 some longer and 2 some shorter).


Lots of fight tweaks to our new Vile Visage! (More are actually coming next patch.)
Repositioned the end of level and bonus timer chests, and gave them some new effects.


SMALL CHANGES:

When exiting an air dash, players now enter the "dash jump" state instead of the "jump" state if the player is still holding down Dash.
Hardcore Challenge teleporters in the hub now first pop up some details on the Skulls involved.
The "Skulls" object in the hub has been replaced with the "Defiant" game mode.

The functionality is effectively identical -- instead of turning on Skulls then starting a Normal game, you just choose the Skulls in Defiant Mode and play there.
Toggling Skulls previously only affected Normal anyway, so this seemed a little more straightforward.
When playing with Skulls on in Defiant Mode, Soul Chip yield is increased (by fidgety numbers we're not sharing publicly yet because they'll probably change).

Marathon and Endless do not give increased SC yields. High Tide counts as 2 Skulls for determining SC yield, and Rock counts as 3.


Eternal Star's Level 8 batbros are now 20% likely to spawn as exploders (down from 100%). They'll also be colored differently.
Adjusted Eternal Star's boss room. It's a little more navigable, and Player 2's HUD won't block the bottom left corner anymore.
The Purist skull now also disables Core Augs. (Core chests are replaced by normal Aug chests.)
Changed the "Soul Foe" glow (pretty drastically) so they no longer appear almost invisible against certain backgrounds.
Two new Augs!
Some Menu changes (mostly cosmetic, for now -- the big Options Patch is probably next patch).
Volume settings now adjust as you scroll, instead of on hitting Confirm.
The end-of-level barrier is now much taller.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed Ace's Glaive not caring about boss invuln while in midair.
Fixed the co-op Power re-map bug.
(hopefully) Fixed a bug causing the occasional invisible enemy. (I think it was introduced in the same patch that added the various room teleporters.)
Fixed a hilarious superjump glitch. (Thank you for tipping me off.)
Fixed a few bugs that could cause clients in online co-op to get locked out of the boss room.


KNOWN ISSUES:

(still) Some minor cosmetic issues with the new Lock icon. (Sometimes it doesn't display on Shop Teleporters when it should.)


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.956b Patch Notes -- July 6, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch retires Arach, makes Skytemple some more fair, and generally tightens up some enemy patterns & item interactions.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Arach's replacement! Skytemple & enemy fairness stuff!

For the next few patches: Narrative work, Frostor targeter changes (hopefully), end of level feel and more!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

The Vile Visage is upon us! (Arach's off hitting the gym.)
Heavily experimental: wall clings now reset movement abilities (double jump, airdash, fly, hover). We've gotten a lot of feedback about this, and while it does make the game a little easier, we're going to try it out.


SMALL CHANGES:

20XX now pauses whenever the window loses focus (if the game isn't already paused, anyway).
Skytemple beams are now *slightly* more forgiving, and the beams themselves have tells when they start/end.
Agnisort's snake enemies now decide which way they'll be spitting their flame at windup time. (No more winding up then turning around suddenly!)
Dracopent's Fang (Head) now stores the last charge attack used, so it'll now store second-level charge attacks (if the player also has Dracopent's Claw).
Dracopent's Fang (Head) now slows the combo decay rate on the Plasma Blender (by 50%).
Dracopent's Fang (Head) now charges up any Rippling Axe attack that comes after an aerial smash.
Snomps (Agnisort snake guys) now decide which way they're spitting at the start of their windup. No more last-second switching!
Lurkers (Vaculab deer-spirit guys) have had their turning center adjusted so they won't instantly swing their faces into flanking players.
Creepers (Frostor spider guys) now have their little light on by default and have a proper idle, so they're easier to spot.
Boss Intros can now be skipped by pressing (jump).
Flapps are now less useless in tight spaces.
Death Lotus no longer triggers his immunity on any repro damage. (Previously it'd trigger on Flamespewer damage.)
Magnetic ceilings now affect the Mortar.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed any of the goofy online co-op bugs that'd cause a boss fight to trigger before actually happening.
Fixed a bug causing local co-op partners to not get Soul Augs before a run.


KNOWN ISSUES:

(still) Some minor cosmetic issues with the new Lock icon. (Sometimes it doesn't display on Shop Teleporters when it should.)


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.955b Patch Notes -- June 22, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch changes the way Repros stack, adds a shiny new font, renames Soul Nuts to Soul Chips (rip), and a bunch of other smaller stuff.

Superfriends: Build coming with Arach's replacement next week!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Repro stacking! New font! New Icons!

For the next few patches: Level design work, boss work (Arach's going on vacation!), narrative work!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Damaging Repros (Bat, Peng, Turret, Dragonface) now level up when you collect more than one, instead of giving you two of the same kind.
Minimechs (floaty guardian Repros) now stack up to 8 (down from infinite). Further pickups instead give 25 nuts. (Having 8 is functionally the same as having 100 anyway, just without the performance hit.)
Lots of changes and tweaks to Frostor/Skytemple level pieces.
New in-game font!
Soul Nuts are now Soul Chips. RIP, Soul Nuts. (Two kinds of nuts ended up being super confusing for new players.)
Mortar now ignores shields. (You'll see why next patch, but we're also moving toward Powers having more utility in general.)


SMALL CHANGES:

Pop-up text for basic pickups (health, energy, etc) no longer shows up once you've unlocked a few things in the Shop.
Sharply reduced the damage Eternal Star takes from Force Nova's chain attacks.
Several new icons!
Health Machines no longer show up for any reason with Famine active.
Fixed up Kur's hitbox some.
Nina's Star Beam now properly allows 3 bursts on screen by default (down from a broken 4).
Eternal Star will no longer fly out of his arena as he sees fit.


BUG FIXES:

The Furor skull is now much more Furor-ious. (Further tweaks may be needed here.)
The roughest Flapps now have a proper coloring (instead of just being confusingly also green).
Be Swift! challenges now properly despawn when failed.
Juiced Shadespurs now orient properly.
Hopefully fixed a goofy issue causing some machines/level-end teleporters to display/collide incorrectly as the client in online co-op.
Fixed an issue where killing the Lunar Astral first could cause their beamlink to persist invisibly until their next teleport.


KNOWN ISSUES:

(still) Some minor cosmetic issues with the new Lock icon. (Sometimes it doesn't display on Shop Teleporters when it should.)


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.8 -> 0.954 Update Summary
notes.content:
BIG CHANGES:

Brand-new boss fights and enemies!
Tons of new items!
Core Augmentations (Core Augs, aka CAs) have been added to the game!

Core Augs affect one of your character's Core Systems -- Body, Head, Arms, and Legs -- granting powerful new abilities.
You can see your current Core Augs both in the Pause screen and visually on your character.
Each Core Aug is exclusive with other Augs in its slot, and each Core Aug belongs to a set.
Core Augs can be mixed and matched with Augs from other sets, but they truly shine when you find a complete set. See what happens!
Core Augs (currently) do not need to be unlocked, and are awarded in Challenge Rooms (always) and Shop Rooms (sometimes).

Challenge Rooms! These rooms optionally spawn as level midpoints. Three waves of enemies stand between you and the door! Each Challenge Room also comes with a bonus Challenge condition. If you achieve it, you'll get a bonus gold chest!
Added Prototype rooms! Discover their glory -- but at what cost?
New item class: Repros! Repros have realized the error of their ways, and want to help you out. Some murder your enemies, some protect you from harm, and some do special, awesome stuff. There are 8 kinds - catch 'em all!
Massive art updates!
Massive game performance updates!
Netcode stability enhancements!
Smarter level design!
Better Challenge scoring and Weekly Challenges!


Thanks for reading!

--

notes.title: 20XX 0.954b Patch Notes -- June 8, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch revamps the game's Shop, Challenge, and Prototype rooms.

NB: Online players, we know the Revive capsules are janky for some of you - we've added a few more robustness fixes to them, but if we still get reports about them not working, we're going to be overhauling the co-op revival system for next patch (June 22). Bear with us!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Shop, Challenge, and Prototype room changes! Some new art!

For the next few patches: Level design work, boss work, narrative work!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Instead of coming across Shops, Prototype Rooms, and Challenge Rooms, players now come across teleporters to these areas. Use the teleporter and you'll go to its respective room.
Teleporters of the same type (for example, two Shop teleporters) will go to the same place, meaning each level can only ever have one Shop, but it may have multiple entrances. (Shops should never have two natural teleporters in the same level, with one exception - see below.)
Boss Hallways now contain an unlockable Shop teleporter - for 5 nuts, you can now visit a shop that you either may have missed, were too poor to buy at before, or whose natural teleporter never spawned in-level. (As mentioned above, this teleporter goes to the same place as the in-level teleporter, so don't expect new items!)
Shops now always contain one Health Machine (in addition to their other stuff).
Challenge rooms are now optional, since you can just walk past the teleporter if you're in a hurry or don't think you have the health to survive it.
Failing a Challenge condition now ends the challenge immediately, allowing the player to use the exit teleporter and despawning remaining enemies. Enemies killed this way can't drop anything and don't count for any "kills" triggers.
Prototype rooms are the only type mentioned here that are relatively unchanged (barring weird cases [read: bugs] where multiple Prototype Teleporters show up in a single level, which shouldn't happen anyway).
0.953's intended hover/fly speed nerfs are now live.


SMALL CHANGES:

Some Skytemple level piece changes. (Not all of them by a longshot!)
Boss Rooms now zoom differently in non-widescreen resolutions to make sure the whole room is visible.
New art for Shadespur, dashing, and vending machines.
Performance improvements for the UI that mostly affect Endless play.


BUG FIXES:

Revive Capsules in online co-op should (hopefully) be far less janky.
Lots of small stuff!


KNOWN ISSUES:

Some minor cosmetic issues with the new Lock icon. (Sometimes it doesn't display on Shop Teleporters when it should.)


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.953b Patch Notes -- May 25th, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch revamps 3 more bosses, adds a character stat display to the pause menu, and a bunch more!

FYI: I'm going to be out of town next week! 0.954b will be accordingly smaller.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: New Eternal Star! New Shatterbeak (shatterwhat?)! Slightly-new Kur!

For the next few patches: Level design work, boss work, narrative work!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Kur rework! This one's lighter than our others. Behold his fairer attack patterns and new mechanic!
Shatterbeak rework! (This is the old Penguin boss.) New mostly-everything!
Eternal Star rework!
The Pause screen now shows your current attack damage, power damage, speed, and jump modifiers.


SMALL CHANGES:

It begins to snow over the chilled Frostor landscape.
Modified *displayed* jump scaling and jump-boost from items. (Nothing has changed - just the way the game displays it.)
Red Slots now always drop something. You'll now get Augs a lot!
Blue Slots have been removed. Nuts are usually better spent elsewhere, anyway.
Hovering and Flying (Armatort/Owlhawk set boots) no longer scale with player speed mods. (Sorry!)
Reduced shop cost scaling slightly. The impact of this is that items are ~6% cheaper at level 1, and ~18% cheaper at level 8.
In Co-op, a player with 0 Max HP now resurrects with 1 armor point instead of dying instantly.
"Chain" effects now occur after a 0.1s delay, so using the Juiced Force Nova in a crowded room will no longer melt your computer.
At Level 8, the Twin Astrals now enrage at half health regardless of whether or not their partner is alive.
Some item names have been changed, but their new icons aren't ready yet - they'll be in next patch.
Ninja Sash speed boost down to 3 (from 4).
Bantam Dancer speed boost down to 1 (from 2).


BUG FIXES:

Twin Astrals can no longer be damaged by attacking their beamchain.
Running over edges at extremely high speeds (not seen in normal gameplay) no longer sometimes improperly sets the "last ground" location you return to after falling.
Fixed the Lotus seeming invulnerable to the client after the first go-around (it was still taking damage; just didn't display it).
Fixed a ton of small bugs.


KNOWN ISSUES:




Thanks for reading!

In Co-op, a player with 0 Max HP now resurrects with 1 armor point instead of dying instantly.
"Chain" effects now occur after a 0.1s delay, so using the Juiced Force Nova in a crowded room will no longer melt your computer.
At Level 8, the Twin Astrals now enrage at half health regardless of whether or not their partner is alive.
Some item names have been changed, but their new icons aren't ready yet - they'll be in next patch.
Ninja Sash speed boost down to 3 (from 4).
Bantam Dancer speed boost down to 1 (from 2).


BUG FIXES:

Twin Astrals can no longer be damaged by attacking their beamchain.
Running over edges at extremely high speeds (not seen in normal gameplay) no longer sometimes improperly sets the "last ground" location you return to after falling.
Fixed the Lotus seeming invulnerable to the client after the first go-around (it was still taking damage; just didn't display it).
Fixed a ton of small bugs.


KNOWN ISSUES:




Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.952b Patch Notes -- May 11, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX brings Ace back down to Earth, introduces some shiny new Gorilla Twins, and fixes a slew of netplay bugs we introduced in 0.951 (as well as several older ones).

NB: Superfriends pals, we've got some good stuff coming sometime during this patch. Keep an eye out!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: New Gorilla Twins! Netplay fixes! Ace balancing!

For the next few patches: Level design work, boss work, narrative work!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Ace normalizations: to compensate for the big boss-damage buffs 0.951's attack group logic gave Ace, we're finally cutting some of the advantages he no longer needs.

Starting bonus damage down to 2 (from 5). This is a 20% reduction in his initial damage, but since he can now full-combo bosses, his boss damage should still be higher than before 0.951.
Jump bonus removed. His jump height is now identical to Nina's.

The Twins reworked! They're deadlier than ever, and now have a new weakness.
Anticipating pending changes to the other four bosses, the boss weakness cycle has been adjusted. Eternal Star and the Twins have swapped weaknesses, as have Arach and the Penguin. The other boss weaknesses remain unchanged.
New SFX for Powers!


SMALL CHANGES:

Enerative Plating +energy on level start up to 4 (from 2).
Shops can no longer spawn the same Core Aug in multiple slots.
Thrift Actuator redesigned. Instead of a 20% stacking discount, this item now makes all items permanently on sale (50% off), but doesn't stack with itself and won't show up more than once in a run. Its in-game shop value has increased to reflect this change.
Beta Cannons (triple shooters) are a little more reasonable when made into Soul Foes.
Toxin timer changes partially reverted - it now only scales the timer when Undying is also active, from 0-20% depending on level.
Added Boss Intros for Perforator/the Twins.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a bug causing the Dracopent set to not work on Ace.
Fixed a bunch of netplay bugs:

Fixed players not having their own boss invuln frames in online co-op.
Fixed Nina's weapons being busted in co-op.
Fixed the boss fight often starting before the intro'd gone away.
Fixed the Host's soul nut augs not working for the client. (We'll still rework this down the line, but at least it works for now!)
Fixed boss HP bars not always functioning well with multiple bosses.
Fixed a certain Vaculab bonus room not spawning properly as client.
Fixed Owlhawk juicing not always working properly as client.
Fixed a bunch of Rollster bugs.
Fixed hypercharge attacks looking goofy.
Fixed a bunch of other stuff!



KNOWN ISSUES:

Still some revive capsule issues in online co-op.
Rollster still slides on walls for some players. We're trying to track this one down!


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.951b Patch Notes -- April 27, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch is relatively small. It introduces the first of our boss intro sequences, makes some changes to Nina's weapons, and more!

NB: Today's patch is on the smaller side, thanks to PAX and the seemingly inevitable PAX Pox that always follows it. We're also using a slightly different patch-number mechanism, since we're quickly running out of numbers before 1.0. Today's patch is 0.951b.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Boss Intros! Nina weapon changes!

For the next few patches: Level design work, boss work, narrative work!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

New "attack group" logic - Weapons that fire multiple bullets and Ace's combo attacks now identify themselves as being part of one group. Changes resulting from this:

Bosses now take damage from a full attack group - if Nina's full Scatterbeam hits a boss, all the pieces do damage. If Ace triple-slashes on a boss, all three hits will connect.
This means the previous vulnerability modifiers for Nina's multi-hit weapons have been removed.
Additionally, Nina's non-Scatterbeam multi-shot weapons (Star, Fork) deal reduced damage for each hit beyond the first, reducing the incentive to jam these weapons in an opponents face for outrageous damage.
We're totally aware that this may do wonky things to balance versus bosses - let us know what you think!

Other Nina weapon changes:

Star Beam damage down to 8 (from 9).
Wave Beam charge attacks now pierce unkilled foes again, but won't hit the same enemy multiple times in a row.
Scatterbeam damage reduced by 20%, but it's still strong vs. bosses since all the pieces now connect.
Fork and Star are now subject to the multi-hit damage penalty, so they're worse at point blank.

Start of our boss intro system implemented (Rollster, Lotus, and a Kur placeholder). The others will come as we finish their reworks.
Vaculab level pass, phase 1.5: It's ~50% done or so. Still missing a lot of pieces.


SMALL CHANGES:

Kur's firewall attack now has a short delay before dealing damage, so it can be nullified by players with the right items or dodged more easily.
Tweaked the screenshake logic. Tell us what you think!
New music after finishing a level!
Repros no longer trigger Death Lotus's hidey-time.
Lots of scaling changes to the new Death Lotus:

Less-tall room from levels 1-4 (5-8 unchanged).
Spawned lotuses have 40% less HP, and don't fire as many mortars at once, making it much more reasonable to find a good spot to hide.
The bottom row of spawns is now better aligned with Nina's basic shot.
The Bonus chest now spawns correctly after the fight.

Few Rollster Beta animation changes.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed an issue where heavy numbers of phase blocks on the screen could cause performance problems.
Powers no longer charge up the Blender's combo status.
Fixed a bug where Death Lotus would fail to retract his deadly vines.
Fixed Shadespur being wonky while wall sliding.
Fixed the Rollster Beta chargequake.
Lots of other small things.


KNOWN ISSUES:



Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.95b Patch Notes -- April 13, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch contains the first steps in our SFX design pass & migration and the first set of Vaculab level changes (maybe 40% or so done). It also reworks the Lotus boss and adds the start of our latest (and hopefully greatest) narrative framework!

NB: Today's patch and the April 27 patch will be on the smaller side -- PAX East is in 9 days, and we've got a ton of work to do to prepare! If you'll be there, we'll be in the Indie MEGABOOTH - come say hi!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Sound Engine Transition (phase 1)! Vaculab Level Design (phase 0.5)! Lotus boss rework (mostly there)! Narrative bits!

For the next few patches: Prepping for PAX, then back to level design work, boss work, narrative work!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Sound Transition, phase 1! We're switching sound engines, and our new sound guy, Ethan (welcome, Ethan!) will be busting up lots of our old sounds and putting in new ones over the next several weeks. Pardon our dust! (We'll be opening a Sound Feedback thread much like our current Bug Report thread.) 
Vaculab level pass, phase 1: It's ~40% done or so. Still missing a lot of pieces.
Lotus boss battle reworked!


SMALL CHANGES:

Donut Lifts (Vaculab's falling platforms) reworked. They now explode/reset upon touching enemies or other solid objects while falling, instead of only ending when hitting a player on the head. Enemies take damage from falling platforms.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed Repros floating back across the stage on level load.
Fixed an issue where Perforator/Rollster would sometimes fail to award bonus chests.
Ace's Rippling Axe causes much less screen shake.
Ace's Rippling Axe and Plasma Blender now gain "charge attack" benefits at appropriate times.
Rollster Beta's difficulty curve adjusted. No longer invulnerable during bounce phase, but moves faster. No longer splits twice before level 8. (Still invulnerable during the two second bounce-attack windup.)
Rollster Beta's Boomerang Blades now rev up for a half second before launching.
Fixed a tutorial issue where the Rollster boss there was way stronger than intended.
Fixed some collision issues mentioned
Fixed a flipped icicle thrower in Frostor.
Fixed players being able to charge attacks while using powers.
Fixed getting around "no attacking!" challenges via charged attacks (but if you charge one up as you enter, that's still okay).
Fixed speed leaderboards generating in "descending" order.
Fixed Rollster/Perf not giving a bonus chest.
Fixed the "evil twin" glitch.
Fixed Slot machines showing health icons for energy wins.
Fixed Slot machines giving health with Famine active.
Fixed issue causing Rollsters to hug corners after their bounce phase.
Fixed Rollsters bouncing off of non-wall things.
Fixed Spirit freezing after player walks away.
Fixed "get under the boss room" exploit (hackishly, by making it harder to get under -- should be impossible now?).
Challenge Skulls now deactivate after returning to the Ark.
Fixed online co-op showing HP as 0 when the character is still alive.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.94b Patch Notes -- March 30, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch brings brings in the first iteration of two of our Boss Rework set (Rollster and Turret). It also reworks all of Ace's alternate primary weapons! We're also brewing up the game's narrative stuff, of which there is one tiny hint in today's build. (The bulk is not ready for prime time yet.)

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Two boss reworks! All of Ace's alternate primary weapons reworked!

For the next few patches: More level design work, boss work, narrative work, boss work!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Turret & Rollster bosses reworked. Turret is 60% different, Rollster is 30% different. We'll continue to iterate on both fights, so give us your feedback!
All of Ace's non-Saber weapons reworked. They should be much more desirable, but they're also now all pretty different. Find your favorite!


SMALL CHANGES:

System Restore no longer cancels out the Sanity Converter's bonus Power damage.
Red Slots now put their additional items to the side.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a bunch of bugs involving interactable machines in online co-op.
Fixed a bug where Thrift Actuators in online co-op caused the host and the client to see different prices.
Fixed a bug where The Rebeginner didn't do very much Rebeginning if the client died in networked co-op.
Fixed a bug where NPCs fall into the abyss if they're near the player when the Crisis Timestopper triggers.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.93b Patch Notes -- March 16, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch is a small one -- mostly fixes and a few more level pieces. It also standardizes a few additional elements of our Daily Challenges so players can compete on a level playing field. A good chunk of this patch period was spent on fancy new boss designs which aren't quite ready to come out of the oven yet.

NB: Since last patch, a number of online co-op bugs have been pointed out that we're looking to fix ASAP, but did not have time to both fix and test in time for today's patch. We're looking to hotfix these fixes in if they can be made fast enough.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Challenge standardization! Fixes! More level pieces! Animations!

For the next few patches: A bunch of online co-op fixes, more level design work, boss work, narrative work.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

More Agnisort level changes.
Reverted floating pickups from 0.92.
Standardized Challenge mode drops for all machines and challenge rooms. (You should now see the exact same drops from health machines, slot machines, and energy machines for a given Challenge, and repeating a Challenge should give the same Challenge Room condition & enemies.)
Lots of little animation changes (and a few major ones).
[Experimental] You can no longer use your primary attack while firing a Power. (You can still alternate, though, and you can hold a charge while using a Power.) Power use currently interrupts Ace's combos.


SMALL CHANGES:

The High Tide skull no longer also increases shop costs.
Red Slots now push out Augments after the first in different places around the machine so they don't get stuck.
Armatort set shoulders are now less overly massive.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a bug where the Choicebooster would screw up RNG consistency in Challenges.
Fixed some scenarios where multiplayer Augs could get stuck in walls/floors.
Fixed a bug causing Shield Drone shields to not be very shieldy.
Fixed some wonkiness with slope movement. (Fiiiinally.)
Fixed a bunch of new tile oddities/invisible blocks.
Fixed Soul Nuts showing up in challenges.
Fixed run stats not counting wins!
Fixed an awesome bug where holding down jump after landing on a slope would make you slooowwwly slide down it.
Fixed an issue where some folks reported Ace not dealing damage if he's the client in online co-op.
Fixed an online co-op bug causing No Damage! challenges to sometimes fail even though neither player seems to take a hit.
Fixed an online co-op bug where on-level items weren't properly doing their job for the client.


KNOWN ISSUES:

Unresolved reports of online co-op sometimes failing to load Agnisort levels -- please report if you still see this!
May be an issue causing framerate drops when the game's been open for awhile. Under active investigation!
Online co-op issues, all of which we're going to try and fix in the next few days:

Some machines still look a little odd.
Juiced Powers (Owlhawk Set bonus) reported not working as client.
Rebeginner reported not working as client.
Machines don't explode on the client, and sometimes can't be used.
Thrift Actuator seems off -- items look like they cost less as Client than they do.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.92b Patch Notes -- March 2, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch has more fixes than anything else, but it also contains the first of a large set of level design changes coming to 20XX. A lot of our current level designs are really dated, and we've learned a lot since we made them, so we're going to revisit many of them and make adjustments (and rework some entirely). In addition, we're making more level piece variants.

The upshot of this should be fairer, more varied, more fun level configurations. This'll take place over the next few patches -- some of Flamelab's changes are up first.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Lots of Agnisort level work! Lots of fixes/tweaks!

For the next few patches: More level design work, boss work, narrative work.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Lots of level design changes to Agnisort, with many more on the way! (Also, some changes elsewhere.)
(experimental) Pickups no longer obey gravity, and instead just bob up and down near where they drop. They also have a small collision radius with each other. (This helps with Slot Machines that can spit out multiple items.)


SMALL CHANGES:

Soul Nuts are now also found at the end of a level, to smooth out SN acquisition some. We've updated many Soul Nut costs accordingly, since they're now more common.
Item unlocks now also grant you the item the first run after you unlock them.
Oxjack's Helm and Thrift Actuators now take effect the level they're picked up (or taken off), instead of only working on future levels.
Oxjack arm-parts reworked. Instead of their weird speed on kill bonus, they now increase player fire rate (by the equivalent of two Bantam Dancers).
Moved the shop item cost scaling factor back two levels (so an item on level 8 will now cost what an item on level 6 would have cost last patch). This results in a 33% drop in costs at level 2, and a ~15% reduction by level 8.
Uncharging Force damage boost increased to +7 (from +4).
Maceknight's retaliation beam (beta models only) now originates from his shield, and has a different color to differentiate it better from Skytemple's other beams.
Rollster Gamma's spawns now share the main one's full vuln table.
System Restore no longer shows up before level 5, and costs 20% less in shops.
Armatort's Dome now lets players overconsume health -- you'll still pick up health while full, in exchange for a chance at picking up armor. (Being at full HP makes getting armor from a health pickup slightly more likely.)
Added on-pickup text for a bunch of items that were missing it.
Prototypes now have slightly different look and feel, and are acquired per-player in co-op. (So your buddy can choose not to take your awful item if he doesn't want it.) They also have a new sound effect! Please pick one up.
20XX now takes Windows' window borders into account when playing in Windowed mode. (This means no more weird squishy bits, because the game will actually run at a slightly lower resolution.)
Added some info to the pause menu (level-theme-boss info & full set bonus if you have it).


BUG FIXES:

Fixed an issue that could cause the Smuggler and the Reflapp to leave the Material Plane, causing them to wreak terrible havoc on every enemy/nut for the rest of the run.
Fixed a bug with Crisis Overdrive where picking it up while already in red health resulted in bad times.
Armor Nut now gives armor for gold nuts (50% chance per).
Fixed a bug causing weird camera issues around the pre-challenge rooms.
Fixed a wonky issue where picking up gold nuts would make a TON of noise lategame.
Fixed an issue locking the game after an ctrl-alt-del or other window loss.
Fixed an issue causing Red Slots to spit out game-crashy garbage.
Fixed the Armorspreader, who lazily failed to correctly spread your armor.
Fixed an issue causing Repros to shoot during the short period after activating a bossgate, but before actually being moved into the boss room (sometimes causing boss instakills).
Fixed an issue causing the Crisis Timestopper to make normally-airborne enemies fall to their deaths after it wore off.
Fixed an issue causing the Skytemple boss music to sound like an old-timey radio.
When swapping characters in the Ark, any already-purchased-takealongs will still display. (Display bug only - you'd still get them on game start.)


KNOWN ISSUES:

Unresolved reports of online co-op sometimes failing to load Agnisort levels -- please report if you still see this!
May be an issue causing framerate drops when the game's been open for awhile. Under active investigation!
Some machines still look a little odd in online co-op.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.91b Patch Notes -- February 16, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today finishes off our set of Item patches (some icons notwithstanding). It also fleshes out a semi-existing item class, the Repros!

NB: Today's patch is a day early. I may not be in the office tomorrow, so I'd rather be a day early than a day late!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: 17 new items! Technical changes! Character balancing!

For the next few patches: Boss work, narrative work.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change. 

--

BIG CHANGES:

New item class: Repros! Repros have realized the error of their ways, and want to help you out. Some murder your enemies, some protect you from harm, and some do special, awesome stuff. There are 8 kinds - catch 'em all!

The existing items Minimech Grinder, Murderdrone, and Skittery Smuggler are three of the Repros. Discover the other five!

12 new Augs (normal ones, not Cores) have been added to the game! Some have placeholder icons.
Character starting stats rebalanced:

Nina now starts with Power Damage +2.
Ace now scales more slowly. His initial combo damage is still 15-15-25, but he starts with Attack Damage +5 with a base of 10, instead of a base of 15.
Ace's charged attacks no longer extend his attack range. Ace is intended as a melee-range character, and his base charged saber felt a little too versatile.
The damage on the rest of Ace's weapons have all been adjusted, and are now better across the board.

The Prototypes now have their own icons! (Finally.)
20XX should use less memory. Endless runs *should* be less likely to crash -- or maybe they'll just crash later. Who knows?
Shop item costs now scale over time. (Toward the endgame, players tend to have tons of nuts right now.)
Items now have rarity ratings that influence how often they show up out of Golden Chests. (Shops are unaffected by this system.)


SMALL CHANGES:

Improved Agnisort loading times, unloading times, and performance. (Tutorial, too, since it uses the same tileset.)
Core Augs now rarely show up from Red Slots (~10%), and Core Chests now rarely replace Gold Chests (also ~10%).
Removed tempstun on picking stuff up.
Reduced enemy density in Skytemple levels.
The Skittery Smuggler no longer spawns in co-op play. (This was never a good idea!)
Added a Stats screen!
The Quint Laser is no longer blocked by the Spider boss's Nova attacks.
Increased the "Be Swift!" time limit to 25 seconds (from 20). Part of this makes up for the recent increase in between-wave time, but we also wanted to make this challenge a little softer.
Don't Attack! challenge rooms now spawn a Large Energy capsule along with the first enemy wave.


BUG FIXES:

Resolved at least one on-level-change crash. (There may be one left -- send us your reports!)
Fixed some memory leaks. (Not 100% sure we've gotten the one(s) that we think were crashing Endless.)
Fixed some Skytemple enemy visual glitches in online co-op.
Clients can now see when items are on sale in online co-op.
Fixed an issue causing boss HP bars to deplete prematurely in online co-op.
Fixed an issue where a player in online co-op could get stuck outside the boss room. (We think!)
Fixed an issue in Endless causing bosses to not fully juice up their HP.
Fixed a bug causing damage equal to your armor to also cost some health.
Fixed a bug causing Soul Nut purchases to stick around when returning to the Ark after a run.


KNOWN ISSUES:

Some machines look a little odd in online co-op.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.90b Patch Notes -- February 3, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch introduces a fancy new item type, the Core Augmentation!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Core Augs! (This is part of our set of Item Patches.)

For the next few patches: The Item Patch (part 2!), boss work, narrative work.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change. 

--

BIG CHANGES:

Core Augmentations (Core Augs, aka CAs) have been added to the game!

Core Augs affect one of your character's Core Systems -- Body, Head, Arms, and Legs -- granting powerful new abilities.
You can see your current Core Augs both in the Pause screen and visually on your character.
Each Core Aug is exclusive with other Augs in its slot, and each Core Aug belongs to a set.
Core Augs can be mixed and matched with Augs from other sets, but they truly shine when you find a complete set. See what happens!
Core Augs (currently) do not need to be unlocked, and are awarded in Challenge Rooms (always) and Shop Rooms (sometimes).
The introduction of the Core Aug system makes some items obsolete (because their abilities are part of the new system). These are:

White Feather
Aerial Stabilizer
Gold Stud
Blood Magic
Energy Armor

While the CA system introduces some new character capabilities into 20XX, it also removes some -- doublejump and airdash currently do not stack (since they're both leg-slot cores). We're aware of the impact this might have on the game, and will do something about it if we decide it's too fun to let go of. (In the meantime, this patch also introduces two new mobility powers, so try those out!)



SMALL CHANGES:

Increased Challenge Room incidence rate (to 60% from 50%).
Nerfed Maceknight attack range. 
Nut-costing Slot Machines nerfed a little -- now slightly less likely to get a passive (down to 15% from 20%). They'll also explode after awarding a passive (and sometimes earlier).
A few items have been renamed in advance of some pending changes. (They'll make more sense next patch.)
Challenge room enemies take an additional second to spawn.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a bug that'd every-so-often cause jumps to fail on Skytemple's moving track platforms.
Fixed an online co-op bug causing slot machines to blow up on the host's side, but not the client's.
Fixed an online co-op bug causing the Maceknight's weapon to display weirdly.
Fixed a co-op bug causing the Shinier Token to grant 6 tokens (instead of 3).
Fixed an issue where the Gobbler (challenges only atm) would chase a falling nut forever, since it's falling faster than the Gobbler can move.
Fixed an online co-op bug causing on-kill effects to be stronger than intended for the client.
(not really a bug) Added some logging code to try to help get to the bottom of the most frequent crash reported by users.


KNOWN ISSUES:

Some machines look a little odd in online co-op.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.89b Patch Notes -- January 20, 2016
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch reworks Fortune Rooms and level-end pieces, adds a new Soul Nut shop, and more!

First, though: I want to thank everyone for being a part of 20XX's time so far on Early Access! Your comments, suggestions, and other feedback have been such an important part of getting the game to where it is today.

As we get closer to 1.0, I'd like to invite you to join our very-slightly-less-public community where we'll be helping spread the word about 20XX when it comes out, as well as offering various surprises, early content, and fun things for being part of the team. If any of that sounds interesting to you, fill out the form below and we'll be in touch soon. Thanks!

Form link: click me!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: New Soul Nut shop! Level end & Fortune Room reworks! Multiplayer/challenge room bugfixes!

For the next patch or two: Boss work, The Item Patch, narrative work.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

A friendly new (placeholder) face is in the Ark. He'll sell you one-time run boosts in exchange for Soul Nuts! 

Items purchased at the upstairs Soul Nut shop give you an Augment for that run only.
In online co-op, the client's Soul Nut shops are ignored.

Level end pieces reworked to flow better.
Fortune rooms removed. Instead, every level ends with a randomly chosen Machine (health, energy, nut-slot, token-slot, or vitality converter).
Removed a provision that prevented an item from spawning if you'd already found one. (This is still in place for items that don't stack.)


SMALL CHANGES:

Pause screen changed up -- added a mysterious blank space that'll be populated soon, renamed Passives -> Augs, expanded space from 40 to 48.
Additionally, you'll now see item-stacking in the pause screen instead of one icon per pickup.
Removed an old tweak that increased your animation speed/footstep rate at higher speeds.
Upgraded how NPCs speak to you.
Force Nova energy cost reduced to 1 (from 2). Damage vs the Twins reduced by 40%. (This is to make up for the change preventing Force Nova from multi-hitting normal enemies -- it no longer deserved its cost penalty.)
Slot machines now properly seed in Challenges.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed an online co-op crash.
Fixed some challenge room bugs that made them wonkily spawn all three waves at once or fail to open.
Fixed a bug causing Skytemple to fail to play boss music sometimes.


KNOWN ISSUES:

The new one-run Soul Shop is wonky in online co-op. It works, but the client will get a little extra stuff. We'll be hotfixing this out tomorrow.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.88b Patch Notes -- January 6, 2016
notes.content:

NB: We've learned that some antivirus software (notably Avast) complains about 20XX when it updates (likely because it's an "unknown" executable). If 20XX fails to start for you, try telling your antivirus software to let it through. Thanks!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Lots of bug fixes and QOL improvements. Fixes to Challenge/Fortune rooms.

For the next patch or two: Boss work, The Item Patch (actually coming next patch!), narrative work.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change. 

Happy holidays!

--

BIG CHANGES:

20XX's resource loading system has been tweaked some.  The game should start faster and use less memory.
Added some network robustness code that should fix missing machines and failing resurrect machines. Also, the client in online co-op can now choose the next level.


SMALL CHANGES:

Fortune Room machines no longer drop tokens (or the passive that gives 3 tokens).
Skytemple's lightning enemies should no longer attack players from outside of challenge rooms. They now no longer agro through walls, but will still move through walls once agro'd or damaged.
A bunch of small Challenge Room tweaks:

Both doors now open when the Challenge is complete (so you can backtrack if you'd like).
The force barrier before the Challenge room and the shot-blocking invisible wall after it now both go away after the challenge is complete.
The camera should be a lot less wonky when finding your character on top of the Challenge room (which is now a-okay to hop on top of, walk over, etc).
The snap-camera now no longer snaps after the challenge is complete (so it'll feel more like a normal room).

Fixed a rare issue where you could get stuck in a Challenge room and the doors wouldn't open.

Fixed Fortune Rooms occasionally dropping items that have been removed from the game.

KNOWN ISSUES:

Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.87b Patch Notes -- December 23, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch introduces polished character skins and introduces the Fortune Room (as well as a new currency, the Token). GLHF!  

NB: This patch and next are affected at least a little bit by the holidays, so sorry if we're a little slow!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Character polish! Fortune Room! Tokens!

For the next patch or three: Multiplayer stability work, boss work, The Item Patch (someday soon!), narrative work. We're also overdue for a basic small-bug-fix-set patch -- we have a few dozen tiny things that should really be fixed that we'll probably spend some time on this coming patch. We've gotten most of our big singleplayer crashes out of the way -- at least, the ones that our reporter sends us -- but there's one happening in online multi, and one game-quit we're still working on. (Send us your log if your game exits on you!)

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change. (These notes feel short -- pretty sure we're missing some smaller stuff. Oops.)

Happy holidays!

--

BIG CHANGES:

New character art & animation polish!
Introducing the Fortune Room! Gamble your life away with three new machines:

The Blue Slot costs two nuts per spin. It'll give you basic pickups! If you're lucky, it'll give you a Passive sometimes, too.
The Red Slot costs a Shiny Token to spin. Its reward pool is much more valuable than the Blue Slot! If you're really, really lucky, it can give you up to 3 items per spin.
The Vitality Converter costs health. Every time you use it, it'll take 1 HP, and give one or more nuts in return. (Sometimes it'll even give a Token!)

Overhauled the boss HP scaling formula. The result is much lower boss HP early, similar boss HP around levels 6-7, and slightly higher boss HP by 8+. We'll continue to monitor this in case we've over-nerfed the earlygame bosses or made Endless/High Tide impossible.
Boss weakness weapons also now scale up over the course of the game (so that with the new lower earlygame boss HP, having the weakness still lets you kill it fast, but not instantly).


SMALL CHANGES:

Changed some level background color schemes to reduce foreground/background confusion. (We have a long way to go on this, though, and these changes are experimental.)
Characters no longer consume health/energy pickups when their max health or energy is zero.
Boss health scaling in co-op reduced to 50% (from 75%).
Spider enemy's HP scaling changed so that Nina's base charged shot kills the basic version. The later versions have about the same HP.


BUG FIXES:

Vending machines in online co-op no longer sometimes charge the user twice. (Finally!)


KNOWN ISSUES:



Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.86b Patch Notes - December 8, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch lands a day early, since I'll be out of the office tomorrow. It adds proper leaderboard scoring, totally revamps our shader system (hopefully improving performance for some users -- tell us!), and adds some quality of life improvements.

NB: We've got some crash issues right now. Our top priority after this patch goes out is solving them, no matter how long it takes. (There will be a hotfix or two sometime in the next few days once we've nailed down the causes.)

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

We've added leaderboard scoring, so this patch resets the all-time leaderboards! The save file will also change a little,  but 20XX should still load your previous save file properly and save over it in the new format.

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Shader performance overhaul! Leaderboard scoring! Other things!

For the next patch or two: Crash fixes, then boss stuff & item patch, lots of boss stuff. Also, other ways to spend nuts & soul nuts.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Leaderboards are now scored as a combination of enemy kills, time on the bonus clock, final nutscore, and remaining HP+Armor (if completed).
Daily challenges are no longer ranked by Time, since Time factors into the overall score.
Revamped pixel shader system from the ground up. Users with potato-based computers should notice a difference in framerate -- please share your experience!


SMALL CHANGES:

Players no longer die from having 0 HP if they still have armor. (This usually happens when picking up the Final Shell, then some other -HP item.)
Automatic attacks (like the shooty familiar) no longer trigger enemy retaliations when blocked.
The Lotus boss can no longer start the fight by lashing to the left.
Normal nuts and soul nuts are no longer displayed together on screen. Normal nuts are now visible during gameplay, and Soul Nuts are visible in the Ark.
The Plasma Blender now triggers a much lower invuln timer on bosses.
Soul Nuts now only display while in the Ark, and regular Nuts only display while in game.
Holding "down" no longer prevents jumping while *not* on drop-through platforms.
The Boss weakness cycle has been adjusted (so it's actually a cycle)! Rollster and Penguin now have different weaknesses.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed an issue causing items that reduce damage to fail to display that in their popup tip.
(Hopefully) fixed an error causing the Change Controls screen to display "255: CONTROL ERROR" as the input device.


KNOWN ISSUES:

The white-fade effect is busted in the Turret boss's stage. We'll fix it soon!


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.85b Patch Notes - November 25, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch introduces another new roomtype: the Prototype room. (The art in the Prototype room is very, very placeholder.) The Prototype room contains a familiar face and the promise of greatness - but at what cost? (This patch contains 10 new items, all of which are only available in Prototype rooms.)

This patch also contains a bunch of fixes, QOL changes, and starts to lay the groundwork for our Big Item Patch.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

(When we change the Scoring mechanism on our leaderboards, we're likely to wipe the all-time boards for both Score and Time. Beware!)

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Prototype Rooms! Bug fixes.

For the next patch or two: Big item patch, lots of boss stuff. A few other ways to spend nuts & soul nuts.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

Happy Thanksgiving! 

--

BIG CHANGES:

Added Prototype rooms! Discover their glory.
Iterated on the enemy placement algorithm. Bats and the like will still swarm, but "big" enemies will now avoid clustering on top of one another in levels.
Boss HP reduced by 25%.
Tweaked boss vulnerability multipliers. In general, the weapon a boss is weak against is now about 50% stronger. Vera does much more damage against most bosses.


SMALL CHANGES:

Built a new on-pickup messaging system. The info you get from picking stuff up is now much more useful.
Reworked the "no jumping!" challenge condition. (You can now jump 5 times before failing.)
"Don't attack!" challenges can't show up before level 3.
Force Nova can no longer multi-hit enemies.
Sound Investments now grants 20% of your nut total on level completion (instead of +10). It stacks with itself (for now).
Damage from falls now resets the Targeter in Frostor.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a bug causing Black Square items to show up now and again.
Fixed a bug where basic Lightning Guys thought they could hit you horizontally. They can't, and now know better.
Damage boosts reworked under the hood. Several items now grant slightly more or less damage, and the scaling's a bit different. 
Finally fixed the weird on-load resolution issues. (This may also take a weird on-startup crash bug with it -- here's hoping!)
Fixed a bug causing Ace to be unable to hit the Spider boss when he's on the ceiling.
Fixed a bug causing client boss health bars to display incorrect info.
Enemies outside of Challenge Rooms will now ignore players during the Challenge Waves.


KNOWN ISSUES:

If you come across an on-startup crash bug, tell us! We think it's related to some of our weird resolution issues, but we currently believe those might be fixed. Let us know!


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.84b Patch Notes - November 11, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch introduces a new room type - the deadly Challenge Room. It'll show up to block your way about half the time, starting on Level 2 of a run.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

(When we change the Scoring mechanism on our leaderboards, we're likely to wipe the all-time boards for both Score and Time. Beware!)

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Challenge Rooms! Bug fixes. (Also a few small bugs that we'll be hotfixing out tomorrow.)

For the next patch or two: Big item patch, lots of boss stuff. More special rooms!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change!

--

BIG CHANGES:

Challenge Rooms! These rooms optionally spawn as level midpoints. Three waves of enemies stand between you and the door! Each Challenge Room also comes with a bonus Challenge condition. If you achieve it, you'll get a bonus gold chest!
Boss health increased. (Big boss changes are still coming!)


SMALL CHANGES:

Powers no longer cost energy once the level boss is dead, allowing players to test freely.
Healthfinder, Enerscoop, and Nut Whisperer reworked. Instead of granting a passive bonus chance to get health, energy, or nuts from slain foes, these items now give a chance for enemies to drop a bunch of their respective resource all at once.
Glass Cannon no longer grants Energy. (It still boosts Damage, Power Damage, and Speed in exchange for two health.)
Shops now contain 4 items after level 3, and 5 items after level 6 (up from 3).
Buttons for your primary/powers now display on the in-game UI.
Scatterbeam now has slightly lower range.


BUG FIXES:

I know I've promised this one before, but the frozen Rollster split bug is finally resolved.
A bunch of other pretty small things!


KNOWN ISSUES:

It's possible to trigger a challenge event if you can get under the challenge room. This won't really help you or break anything, but you'll probably fail the challenge.
In online co-op, Boss health bars show the wrong amount of health (they'll show as empty too early).


Thanks for reading!

Lotsa little things.

notes.title: 20XX 0.82b Patch Notes - October 14, 2015
notes.content:

For the next patch or two: Lots of enemy changes (visual and mechanics). Starting our big Boss overhaul, aimed at making 20XX's bosses a more important, enjoyable, and memorable part of the game. Item stuff! Leaderboard scoring & polish.

--

BIG CHANGES:

We've made some changes to our renderer that should improve framerate stutter for folks. If you previously had poor 20XX performance, tell us if it's any different!
Lots of new art:

Crates of all kinds have new art/levels of destruction as you bust 'em open!
Frostor's icicle shooters have proper art! The icicle they fire is now also used for Splinterfrost.
The glorious Earth (or is it?) is now visible in the Ark/Menu!
Vaculab's falling platforms have updated art!
Vaculab's falling platforms no longer push players through the world forever -- instead, one falling on your head will break the platform, and you'll take damage.

Late game Cannon enemies now triple-shoot (but half as fast).

Skytemple Boltpairs now have a thinner collision fixture, making them a little more forgiving.
Lategame conveyor belt speed now scales more slowly.
Many enemy attacks that previously scaled with level no longer do.
Shrunk the size of some explosions & the item pickup effect (so they no longer eat up the screen).

Fixed a bug causing Weekly timed challenges to display in reverse order.
Fixed a bug causing items in online co-op to occasionally dupe if both players pick it up at once.
Fixed a bug causing your Resolution choice to fail to save.
Fixed a loooong-standing bug allowing you to jump twice without double jump if your second jump was within 100ms of your first.
Fixed the "Killed By" field occasionally saying wrong things.

Fixed a visual glitch where a level chunk could disappear as you got to the far edge of the next room.
Fixed a crash occurring in very high level Endless runs. (There is a good chance there are other ways high level Endless runs can crash. Play at your own risk!)
Fixed a bug allowing a player whose online partner has left mid-run to be joined by someone looking for a random partner. (This ended up with one person in game and one person in the lobby and two irritated players.)

Casual item selection in online co-op behaves a little strangely. (It works, but the menus get a bit spinny.)
Hitting back on a controller in the Casual/Netplay menus while in an active multiplayer session sometimes causes the menu to instantly reappear.


Thanks for reading!
