notes.title: 20XX 0.81b Patch Notes - September 30, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch adds a bunch of Challenge support, and cleans up some of the issues that we've noticed since our Beta release. It also adds a few new toggle-able options, so today's patch will reset your options (but not keybinds).

Note: We changed a ton about 20XX's Challenge system this patch. There will almost certainly be bugs; we'll fix them as fast as we can!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

(When we change the Scoring mechanism on our leaderboards, we're likely to wipe the all-time boards for both Score and Time. Beware!)

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Challenge stuff (co-op + speedrunning + weeklies). Endless Skull. Resolution fixes, a few performance enhancements.

For the next patch or two: We're mostly focused on polishing the presentation of what we've got. Lots of environment art/object art coming soon!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change!

--

BIG CHANGES:

New Skull -- Endless: the game goes on forever and ever and ever until you die. Disables Leaderboard stuff. (Disclaimer: Game may break at incredibly high levels. No promises!)
Tons of new Challenge stuff:

All challenges are now also co-op accessible, and have their own Leaderboards. Each Steam account can do each Daily co-op challenge once a day, whether it's done online or locally.
Time challenges! Each challenge is now scored twice, based both on time and on score. At the end of a run, your score gets uploaded to both boards if you survive the run (and only to the Score board if you die).
Weekly challenges! The Weekly challenge resets every 7 days on Wednesday, and can be repeated as many times as a player likes. The Weekly challenge is geared toward optimizing a given set of levels (read: speedrunning).
All challenges now have fixed level orders -- no more choosing. (This may be a contentious one, but the runs were awfully non-fixed choosing different level orders would generate different stuff! This was intended from the get go, but was a little busted.)
In a soon-to-come patch (but not this one), the Nut-scored challenges will be scored more comprehensively. 
The bug where you have to switch pages to get the Leaderboard you're looking at to show the right data has been fixed.

In co-op, players now share nut totals. (The double display will be removed next patch.)
Greatly improved game performance around liquids (and a few overall tweaks that should make life better on lower-end systems).
Resolution changing actually works properly now.


SMALL CHANGES:

Casual Mode now describes the items you're choosing.
Added a force barrier to the ends of levels you'd otherwise be able to jump over.
Splinterfrost now works correctly. (It's been semi-busted for so long that it might feel totally different!) Its numbers have been adjusted to keep its overall power in line with the busted version.
Bullets now properly die upon contact with walls (instead of inside walls).
Reduced Vera's damage vs. most bosses by 50%. (We'll keep an eye on this; this may be too severe a nerf -- the damage vs. Kur has been reduced by 40%.)
Spillover Matrix has eaten a healthy swing of the nerf bat. It no longer gives health when excess energy is found (and now only goes the other way). To compensate, it now grants twice as much energy per point of health, and costs 25% less in shops. Rationale: Spillover was too powerful, and actively discouraged the use of Powers.
Tinkered with some earlygame level pieces to make them less punishing.
Enemy density scaling (after level 3) has been tweaked downward.
Slowed Nina's run animation a bit and fixed the footstep sounds.
The Turret boss no longer sometimes starts his circle attack right as the fight starts (potentially firing right at the entrance).


BUG FIXES:

Fixed two crash issues.
Fixed a bug causing the Daily Challenge to be playable multiple times in a day.
Fixed a bug causing players to fall off of a magnetic ceiling in a particular Vaculab level piece.
Fixed some out-of-sync footstep sounds.


KNOWN ISSUES (to be fixed really soon):

Casual item selection in online co-op behaves a little strangely. (It works, but the menus get a bit spinny.)
Hitting back on a controller in the Casual/Netplay menus while in an active multiplayer session sometimes cause the menu to instantly reappear.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.80b Patch Notes -- September 15, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch marks our official Beta release. It includes a visual and mechanical revamp of Frostor, a new Casual mode, and much more!

Big thanks to the Community for helping us test this one before it went live!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in beta. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

The all-time leaderboards will be wiped with this patch - your save files will not. If you want to reset your save, go into your Documents folder -> 20XX -> delete "20xxalphav64.sav".

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: So, so much. Big Arctech revamp. Casual mode! A million other changes.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change!

--

BIG CHANGES:

A new mode has been added (Casual), aimed at smoothing the getting-into-20XX experience out a bit.

Casual mode runs begin with the player choosing three of his unlocked passives to start with. Any three! No duplicates.
Casual mode runs are not Leaderboard-eligible.
Casual mode is available for any number of players (local or online). In online co-op, whatever the host picks is also awarded to the client.
Normal mode awards slightly more Soul Nuts than Casual.

Arctech (Frostor) has received one million changes.

Complete visual overhaul! (There's still a lot of tiling polish to do.)
Many/all level bits have been cleaned up, improved, or totally overhauled.
Enemy placement diversification +1000%.
New Hazard: Motion Traps (name pending). They're basically flame geysers that only trigger when you pass in front of the trap.
Teleporters now transport the player much faster.
Targeters now reset when the player takes damage, preventing the terrible double-whammy scenario. This includes fall damage. (The actual rule is "the targeter can't target the player during his invuln frames.")
Targeter damage no longer scales (capped at 1).
Beta Creepers (late-game exploding spiders) no longer also explode on death.
All Creepers now explode much faster once activated.
Penguins now require line of sight to start dashing at the player.




SMALL CHANGES:

Kur's fire breath attack now only fires off one salvo before level 5.
Kur's Quintlaser attack now fires 2 cubes before level 5 (down from 3). The cubes now move 25% faster at all levels.
Death Lotus now no longer damages players that bump into him while he's hiding.
Touching lava (and lava-like things) now sends the player back to his last safe landing, even if the player has recently taken damage (in which case no further damage is incurred).
Starting the Daily Challenge/Hardcore no longer clears your Soul Nuts. Additionally, Soul Nuts no longer display during challenges.
Added a "really continue?" prompt when you try to start a game in Normal/Casual, but could still afford to buy something with your Soul Nuts. This prompt does not trigger during online play.
Added tooltips for the various game modes and for the Skulls menu.
Added in some bonus Skytemple level pieces!
Improved the corner of Skytemple's track platforms that'd bump you upward as the platform changes direction. (It still wobbles a tiny bit.)
Revamped the boss gate visual.
Dialogue/Lore's taking a nap until we're sure of how to do it right.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a bug causing Rollster Gamma's late-game split ability to produce lame offspring.
Fixed a bug causing the Mace Knight's shield to continue to block Ace's attacks for a bit after the shield falls.
Fixed an issue where lategame bosses with Undying would bug out the boss HP bar.
Fixed a bug causing Ace's Axe to deal no damage in net co-op if the player is not the host.
Fixed a bad platform assignment in Skytemple that could make a jump pretty much impossible without upgrades.
Fixed a bug where Casual items wouldn't show for your ally in online play.
Fixed a crash if you didn't choose 3 items in online Casual play.
Fixed a bug where Frostor had too many enemies lategame.
Fixed every chunk and missing platform/tile/etc mentioned so far between everyone's screens -- gonna spend a few hours today grinding through it to find more myself!
Fixed a bug making Skulls work in casual.
Fixed a bug causing Arctech to use the wrong color swap after level four (shouldn't be red anymore!)
The new Penguin Boss sometimes gets a saw blade stuck in his mouth. (fixed)
One Arctech chunk has been disabled (due to not being tiled yet). (fixed)
The drop-down tooltips at level starts and boss fights will have a boss portrait accompanying them; they don't yet. (fixed)
Arctech's End Chunk teleporters display a little oddly. (fixed)


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.785a Patch Notes - September 14, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch gets the game where we want it as we head into beta. This includes a huge visual (and less huge mechanical) update to Frostor, a new mode, and more!

We're pushing this patch a little early to give the community time to break it before the 15th. :)

We'll be updating these patch notes until the 15th, when the beta officially launches.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in alpha (OR IS IT??). As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

We will almost certainly be wiping save files (or at least, invalidating them) when beta launches. We'll probably wipe the all-time Leaderboards, too.

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: So, so much. Big Arctech revamp. Casual mode! A million other changes.

For the next patch or two: Beta stuff.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change!

--

BIG CHANGES:

A new mode has been added (Casual), aimed at smoothing the getting-into-20XX experience out a bit.

Casual mode runs begin with the player choosing three of his unlocked passives to start with. Any three! No duplicates.
Casual mode runs are not Leaderboard-eligible.
Casual mode is available for any number of players (local or online). In online co-op, whatever the host picks is also awarded to the client.
Normal mode awards slightly more Soul Nuts than Casual.

Arctech (Frostor) has received one million changes.

Complete visual overhaul! (There's still a lot of tiling polish to do.)
Many/all level bits have been cleaned up, improved, or totally overhauled.
Enemy placement diversification +1000%.
New Hazard: Motion Traps (name pending). They're basically flame geysers that only trigger when you pass in front of the trap.
Teleporters now transport the player much faster.
Targeters now reset when the player takes damage, preventing the terrible double-whammy scenario. This includes fall damage. (The actual rule is "the targeter can't target the player during his invuln frames.")
Targeter damage no longer scales (capped at 1).
Beta Creepers (late-game exploding spiders) no longer also explode on death.
All Creepers now explode much faster once activated.
Penguins now require line of sight to start dashing at the player.




SMALL CHANGES:

Kur's fire breath attack now only fires off one salvo before level 5.
Kur's Quintlaser attack now fires 2 cubes before level 5 (down from 3). The cubes now move 25% faster at all levels.
Death Lotus now no longer damages players that bump into him while he's hiding.
Touching lava (and lava-like things) now sends the player back to his last safe landing, even if the player has recently taken damage (in which case no further damage is incurred).
Starting the Daily Challenge/Hardcore no longer clears your Soul Nuts. Additionally, Soul Nuts no longer display during challenges.
Added a "really continue?" prompt when you try to start a game in Normal/Casual, but could still afford to buy something with your Soul Nuts. This prompt does not trigger during online play.
Added tooltips for the various game modes and for the Skulls menu.
Added in some bonus Skytemple level pieces!
Improved the corner of Skytemple's track platforms that'd bump you upward as the platform changes direction. (It still wobbles a tiny bit.)
Revamped the boss gate visual.
Dialogue/Lore's taking a nap until we're sure of how to do it right.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a bug causing Rollster Gamma's late-game split ability to produce lame offspring.
Fixed a bug causing the Mace Knight's shield to continue to block Ace's attacks for a bit after the shield falls.
Fixed an issue where lategame bosses with Undying would bug out the boss HP bar.
Fixed a bug causing Ace's Axe to deal no damage in net co-op if the player is not the host.


KNOWN ISSUES:

The new Penguin Boss sometimes gets a saw blade stuck in his mouth.
One Arctech chunk has been disabled (due to not being tiled yet).
The drop-down tooltips at level starts and boss fights will have a boss portrait accompanying them; they don't yet.
Arctech's End Chunk teleporters display a little oddly.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.77a Patch Notes - August 19, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's patch introduces 20XX's first flavorful lore bits in the form of boss dialogues. It also gets Skytemple closer to where we want it to be, and makes the 20XX endgame a little softer in general.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in alpha. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Skytemple debt, boss dialogues, endgame softening.

For the next patch or two: Small things. We'll be showing 20XX at PAX Prime in just ten days! Preparing for the show and then actually showing the game'll take a lot out of us, so expect a small one for next time.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Added the first chunk of our boss interactions (read: story bits) system. The accept button rapidly scrolls through the text; the back button skips it entirely. Ace and Nina each have their own unique dialogue, which'll be expanded on greatly in future patches.

Interactions don't trigger during online play or during challenges. In local co-op, they trigger based on whoever's first player. (We might add special co-op dialogue down the line!)
NB: we're not writers. Tell us if it sucks, and we'll hire somebody!

Paid off our Skytemple debt, including:

Cannon enemy reworked + new art!
More level pieces we hadn't finished prior to last patch!
Nerfing some of the unfairly-hard level setups!
Tracks for the track platforms! (readability++)
Tweaks to the Mace Knight and the Boltmans!



SMALL(ER) CHANGES:

Nerfed the White Feather. Air jumps are now more like air hops (~50% of a normal jump), and don't take you up a full jump height. (That was ridiculous, and we should have changed it months ago.)
Plumber Hat jump boost reduced by ~33%. (It's still really good.)
Spike-type objects and falls now deal 1 damage after level 4 (down from 2).
Adjusted the enemy density formula so that fewer enemies spawn by endgame. (By level 8, 25% fewer enemies should spawn.)
Adjusted the enemy density formula to avoid unfairly populating certain Skytemple segments.
Increased the Boomerang Blade's base damage by 33%.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed some weird boltpair interactions in Skytemple.
Fixed a weird platform-reset bug where wind platforms could go bonkers if you left a room and came back.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.76a Patch Notes - August 7, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch brings Phase 1 of our Skytemple revamp. (Finally!) Almost everything about the stage has been redone (mechanics, art, enemies), and the parts that haven't been redone are going to be next patch. While we still have a little to go for the rework, we feel that this Skytemple is still a *lot* better than the one in game now, so we'll push it as is. The patch also adds a few more loading speed enhancements.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in alpha. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Skytemple rework, loading improvements.

For the next patch or two: Skytemple debt (cannon enemy, a few chunks, track platform art), enemy tweaks/revamps, starting Arctech rework.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed a change.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Skytemple has been heavily reworked. It is no longer a garbage zone where fun goes to die.

Wind zones have been removed from the game.
Falling blocks (the Skytemple kind) were mostly removed months ago, and their last remaining bits have now been swept away.
Wind platforms have taken the old wind zone's place. These platforms have small fans under them, which, at certain intervals, blast them into the sky with a gust of air.
Boltpairs have filled Skytemple's hazard gap. Each pair fires a dangerous bolt of energy between them either continuously or at intervals.
The old Boltmans foe has been reworked. He has new art, and now fires a vertical blast when he senses a player in range. (No more weird target-y + bolt on contact attack.)
The Mace Knight foe has been reworked. It's mostly a visual upgrade and a nerf to his effectiveness -- his mace now goes further, but only horizontally. (No more aiming.)
(DEBT) The cannon enemy will be reworked by next patch.
(DEBT) Track platforms will be receiving a visual update and some better indicators of where the path is by next patch.
(DEBT) A few chunks aren't ready for today, and will be in place by next patch.
(DEBT) One chunk was tiled by a programmer. Can you figure out which one?!

20XX's levels will load somewhat faster now. This is a continuation of a series of loading improvements that *should* culminate in the game loading acceptably fast.


SMALL CHANGES:

We've added a new visual indicator for the end-of-level teleports: a statue of the boss the teleporter leads to. This way, the player doesn't have to stand on each teleporter before deciding where to go.
Tweaked the Really Quit? options to use our new button graphics instead of raw text.
The character change pods can no longer be activated by a player that's currently using them.
You can no longer character change to your current character.
Adjusted some of the more difficult late-game Agnisort configurations.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a bug causing air dashing to behave weirdly if you were holding jump still when you started the dash.
Fixed a bug where if you dash-jumped off a wall, you couldn't airdash (even if you hadn't airdashed since touching the ground).


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.75b Patch Notes - July 22, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch adds a bunch of new art, some tutorial tweaks, and entirely new Ark/level end chunk bits. (It's a pretty small patch -- there's a lot we're working on for Skytemple that we can't show off yet!)

Disclaimer: 20XX is in alpha. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Several new art assets, tutorial/ark polish, new level end pieces, a few new passive upgrades.

For the next patch or two: Skytemple full rework, load time improvements.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes.

--

BIG CHANGES:

20XX should now load a little bit faster. This is the beginning of a series of loading improvements that *should* culminate in the game loading acceptably fast.
Added a new item class: familiars. (Name subject to change.) Familiars are passive upgrades that orbit your character, having some beneficial effect. Today's patch introduces two such familiars. More are coming.
The Ark has been re-overhauled.
Level end pieces have been overhauled. More readability for the end portals is coming later in this patch.


SMALL CHANGES:

Lotsa HUD tweaks.
New Character select art/teleporter art. (To change characters, just use that color's pod -- no more char select menu!)
Boss-spawned enemies no longer drop anything.
20XX now creates a folder in your My Documents folder, "20XX", and puts its files there instead of just littering stray files in your My Documents folder. Sorry about that. The first time you load this patch, 20XX will load your existing file in its existing location, and then save it to the new location and read it there from then on.
The default size of each health/energy block has been increased.
Added a UI Scale option that we'll refine later. Making it too big will cause unpleasantness in Multiplayer (for now).
Lots of menu system changes:

Pause, Back, and Accept are now rebindable.
No two keys that you could use at the same time can be mapped to the same button. (Everything but Accept/Back can be used at the same time; so Accept/Back can share keys with other functions, but nothing else can. Accept/Back also can't share a key between themselves. All this was done to prevent a bunch of awful goofy menu stuff where one key could get bound to move up and move down by a user who's fiddling with how broken he can make the menu, resulting in a user who can't use or fix the menu without a separate input device.)
If you try to map a key that's already taken, it'll switch with whatever had it. (Using default controls, if I try to map Power 1 to A, it'll recognize that Jump currently has A, and swap the default Power 1 key with it, resulting in Power 1 using A, and Jump using Y.
This is how this should have gone from the start -- folks with nonstandard controllers, please chime in and let us know how it works for you.



BUG FIXES:

Fixed a bug with the Wrath skull.
Fixed a few minor netplay glitches. (A few still remain.)


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.74 Patch Notes - July 8, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch adds a ton of new Menu/UI art and feel (real Boss Healthbars! A good pause screen/death screen! finally). It also adds some more level pieces and fixes a few boss issues.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in alpha. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Massive UI/Menu overhaul (part 1). More level pieces for Agnisort/Vaculab. Lots and lots of tweaks and fixes.

For the next patch or two: Skytemple full rework, More boss work, more level variability, safehouse rework part 2, UI rework part 2.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes.

--

BIG CHANGES:

The Pause menu has been entirely reworked (work in progress). You can select your Powers to move them to other slots (if you pick up a Power and decide you'd rather have it on a different button).
All menus now use fixed Accept/Back buttons (A/B on a controller, Space/Z on keyboard). They're no longer bound to Jump/Interact. That felt bad.
The main menu has been redone.
The death menu has been redone (super work in progress). It'll list a bunch of stats involving how you died and how your run went (to be later integrated into bigger stats that carry across runs).
The in-game HUD has been redone.
Boss health bars now occupy a fixed part of the screen. There may be issues with multi-part boss health bars in networked play for now (we'll fix it).


SMALL CHANGES:

Made a camera change (experimental and not quite done) around level edges to prevent some weird camera issues.
Move speed/attack speed items now also increase the character's animation speeds by an appropriate amount.
Fixed lots of font stuff. Changed the $ sign to a more-fitting nut symbol.
More boss tweaks.
Changed around some controller bind stuff for folks that use non-360 controllers.
The placeholder Shopkeep in the Ark is still a placeholder. Sorry! His overhead message has been updated to reflect the fact that we are sorry about this.
20XX has a new Desktop icon.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a crash some users experienced versus Arach.
Fixed 85 million other small things.


Thanks for reading!

notes.content:

Disclaimer: 20XX is in alpha. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The current price of 20XX ($9.99) will increase to $11.99 when the netplay is stable. We believe we're ready to raise the price, but we want to make sure Netplay is stable first. It could happen tomorrow, or it could happen in two weeks (or any time in between). We want players to be happy with what they're buying; while the game is incomplete, we charge an incomplete price. The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Netplay fixes! Power system change (part 1). More boss changes. 

For the next patch or two: More boss work, more level variability, safehouse rework part 2, UI rework.

On the horizon (extremely subject to change): ????

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes.

--

BIG CHANGES:

We've fixed most of what ailed Netplay. (Details in the bug fixes section.)
We've revamped how Power acquisition and use works in 20XX. (This is experimental, so complain away if you hate it.)

At the end of a level, players now get to choose between the boss's Power, a basic stat upgrade, or a Nutstack (10 nuts). When one's picked up, the others will poof.
In multiplayer, each player gets to make his own choice. Unlike normal upgrade pickups, these will only apply to the choosing player. (This way, you don't have to keep the same Power set as your partner, and you don't get a bonus reward if you take a Power and your partner takes a stat boost.)
Players now only have 3 Power slots; trying to pick up a fourth will drop one.
Powers can be picked up with the Interact button (default B on controller, A on keyboard), or with the Power buttons themselves. If you use a Power button, the new Power will go into that slot (potentially placing your old power in that slot on the ground). If you use the Interact button, the Power will go into the first free slot it finds (swapping with the last slot if all three are full).
All three are bound by default. No more cycling. (Default Controller keys: Y, LB, LT | Keyboard: Q, W, E)
Changing around between lots of weapons a) sucks, and b) doesn't allow for much player choice. We think this (admittedly pretty large) change resolves both of those concerns.

Revamped the Safehouse, which we're going to start calling the Ark, for reasons that'll become clear as we flesh out more story bits. The Ark contains some locked off sections that aren't active yet.
Tutorial has received a facelift.
Added some great new crash reporting stuff. Thanks for your reports! They're amazing.


SMALL CHANGES:

Added a new font in lieu of the old Press Start 2P. (We're working on this one, so font commentary is welcome.)
Many more boss tweaks.
Added a "really quit?" prompt to prevent accidental game quits.
LT/RT are now recognized by the game on a 360 controller. (This may open up options on other controllers.)
Updated the Boomerang's tooltip to reflect that it can be thrown in any direction.
Shopkeeps now say stuff.
Added a placeholder Shopkeep for a super-secret second Soul Nut Shop in the Ark. (It'll be used to buy items that you can take with you into the next run.)
Changed network trust to allow each player to independently report damage taken; the host no longer assigns damage to the client based on where the host thinks the client is.
Made network data fetching faster. (I have no idea how much faster.) Also reduced the volume of traffic being sent substantially.
Nerfed the Energy Armor/Spillover Matrix interaction.
Removed the 0.5s stun on pickup in multiplayer (for now). Some weird bugs related to getting stunned at inopportune times.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed an issue where if you chose Find Game, then Local Co-op, then launched, the game would think you had a partner online and do all sorts of unwanted things. (Choosing Local Co-op now correctly drops you from your lobby.)
Smoothed client positioning.
Fixed an issue causing the camera to fail to reset properly after a netplay level.
Fixed an issue causing Arach to have stale moves.
Fixed a bug where the client doesn't spend nuts on store purchases.
Added a potential fix for Wall Nina.
Fixed a Rollster Beta/gamma display issue where his eye was awfully dull.
Fixed a display issue where the player doesn't disappear when being teleported.
Fixed an issue where a level could spawn with multiple shops, and at least one would be empty.
The new Spider enemies didn't properly blink in the client.
Enemy shields didn't always work correctly on the client.
Skytemple Power drops show up in the wrong spot.
Main Menu Community/Changelog buttons do wonky stuff.
Fixed a game-ending bug in Skytemple where the player is pushed out of the end of the level.
Fixed bugs causing characters to be locked in the "hit" state.
Fixed bugs involving permanent stun while using teleporters.
Fixed a bug where a client with Blood Magic stuns himself sometimes.
Fixed an Energy Armor bug making players invulnerable.
(fixed) Penguins don't rotate correctly on the client's machine.
(fixed) Flash Freeze targeting reticules in Frostor sometimes display improperly.
Fixed an issue where charged/health nuts could kill you.
Fixed a bug where sometimes stuff got duplicated on the client.
(fixed) Clients purchasing from Health/Energy machines are sometimes charged double.
Fixed a bug causing Boss titles to sometimes display incorrectly.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.72b Patch Notes - June 11, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch adds a lot, including online multiplayer. It's currently restricted to 2 players, one per machine. Read on for the full notes.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in alpha. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware!

Note: The current price of 20XX ($9.99) will increase to $11.99 when the netplay is stable. This will likely occur in 2-4 weeks (1-2 patches). We want players to be happy with what they're buying; while the game is incomplete, we charge an incomplete price. The closer we get to release, the closer the price will get to our planned Full Release price of $15.

TL;DR for today's patch: Netplay! Lots of boss changes. Performance enhancements. New Agnisort chunks. Chunk variability system.

For the next patch or two: Boss work, more level variability, safehouse rework, UI rework.

On the horizon (extremely subject to change): ????

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Netplay is live!

It is still in a VERY early state. It will have bugs. 
Probably lots of bugs. 
Current Netplay User Friendliness Rating: 0/10
We've fixed most of the bugs we know about, though, so tell us what you find!
Please report bugs in this community thread.
Netplay is currently 2P only (one per machine).
Netplay currently supports two modes; invite a Steam friend, and find a random partner.
Random partner finding will see if anyone's waiting for a partner, and if not, will have you wait for a partner. This lobby shouldn't time out, but it's our first release, so if you don't find anyone after a few minutes, try again.
The Daily Challenge/Hardcore are unavailable while networked with another player.

All multiplayer stuff is now handled at the Multiplayer portal (teal) in the Safehouse. Accordingly, the two Main Menu options for single/multiplayer have been merged into one Play option.
Several bosses have new art and new/modified mechanics:

The Twins have new art/animations. Their Flameshield ability now only affects one of them per cycle, and times out before teleporting. If encountered after level 4, killing one will cause the other to enrage.
Rollster has new art, a new ability, and his room has been changed.
Flowery Death (Lotus Boss) has been super reworked.
Svalinn Gamma, Shield-Summoner-y boss, has been replaced by Arach, the Predator. It still currently drops Force Nova.
 
We've made a major enhancement to the way we process some animated level pieces; some players will notice better performance. We're still working on this.
This patch contains the beginning of a major level variability rework. Eventually, all chunks will have more room for hazard variability depending on where in the game they're loaded. Today, some chunks have this, many don't.
Several new level chunks have been added for Agnisort, all of which have the new chunk variability setup.


SMALL CHANGES:

Added a new Agnisort platform, a thin (drop-through-able) moving platform.
Energy Armor reworked; no longer absorbs damage at the cost of HP - now restores some energy upon taking damage. The previous version of the item ended up being pretty negative in the late-game, as just a few hits would completely deplete the user's energy bar.
Altered Forest Spirit's aggro radius to prevent players being blasted from offscreen in some starts.
Added black dropshadows to most text, making it easier to read. (Goodbye, white-on-light-color text.)
Main menu's options are now normal text. We're replacing them pretty soon anyway -- pardon the dust.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a bug occasionally causing moving platforms to desync in singleplayer.
Fixed a bug with the new control rebind scheme that could cause the game to incorrectly detect your input device on first boot, causing any control reassignment to hang the game.
Fixed a bug where bosses weren't using their alternate abilities properly.
Fixed a poorly-designed-control (not a bug!) that occasionally caused control-rebinding players to discover the L key, which reloaded our shaders for debug purposes but gave no indication of this, instead just making it look like the game hung for a few seconds. The L key no longer does this, and the developer responsible has been sacked.
Fixed a few issues involving sound effects (armor pickup, Frostor freeze targeter).
Reinstated the above sacked developer after remembering that it was me.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.70b Patch Notes - May 13, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's 20XX patch adds the Level Choice system (pick your next level from 3 choices!) and vastly improves our controller detection/keybinding system. (Choose which input device to use! Have separate keybind sets per player!) It also tweaks a whole lot of numbers and reverts an old Ace nerf.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in alpha. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware! Note: in this patch, we're removing any saved keybind info you have, since we rewrote some control setup code. Feel free to delete your eridu.key file. 

TL;DR for today's patch: Keybind/controller selection scheme rewrite. Level selection system.

For the next patch or two: Netplay, boss work, power work/finalization, more level variability.

On the horizon (extremely subject to change): Safehouse rework, UI rework.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Added the level choice system. At the end of every level, the player will be presented with three portals instead of one, each with a specific boss and level theme.  This gives the player some power to select his path through the game's levels according to what powers he already has and which bosses he wants to take out early or save for later. As the player closes in on level 8, the choices will narrow down (levels 1-5 allow 3 choices, level 6 allows 2, and level 7 has one portal "choice" at the end.)
Much of the control and keybind system has been rewritten. Each player may now choose his own control scheme. 20XX will now detect up to 4 DirectInput devices (up from 2). Players can also now choose which input device to use from the Change Controls menu (which now has a separate menu for P1 and P2). (We've also swapped keybind filenames -- we're now saving "20xxv70alpha.key" to your My Documents folder. You can safely delete eridu.key.)
If your controller doesn't immediately work, you're probably set to the keyboard. Change it in the Change Controls menu!


SMALL CHANGES:

Reverted Ace's 20% damage nerf from a few patches ago. (Relative to last patch, Ace now deals 25% more damage.)
Ace now begins the game with 10 HP (up from 8).
Turret Boss's whirl attack now spins less quickly.
Shield Drones (Alpha version only) will now drop their shield after counterattacking twice.
Reduced the Twins' health by 20%.
Rebalanced Power Boost, and the items that grant it, as follows:

Each point of Power Boost is back to granting 20% damage per point. 
If the player has negative Power Boost (for example, if your first pickup is XCALBER), the penalty per point is 10% (instead of 20% -- last patch, the penalty was a full 30%).
A-Matic now grants 2 Power Boost (up from 1).
In addition to its other effect, Blood Magic now grants 1 Power Boost.
In addition to its other effect, Enerscoop Alpha now grants 1 Power Boost.

In addition to its other effect, Healthfinder 8000 now grants 1 Max HP.
Panther enemies no longer have a weird semi-invulnerability before revealing themselves.
Shield Drone (Frostor) HP reduced by 30%.
Penguin (Frostor) HP reduced by 20%.
Creeper (Frostor) HP reduced by 40%.
Cannon (Skytemple) HP reduced by 15%.
Maceguy (Skytemple) HP reduced by 30%.
Boltfly (Skytemple) HP reduced by 25%.
These are not the big Skytemple/Frostor changes we're working on-- just temporary fixes, since the work on these levels is a little further down our pipeline.


BUG FIXES:

The Twins' Flameshield projectiles had larger hitboxes than their graphic. This has been fixed.
Fixed an issue where Svalinn Gamma (Frostor shield boss) would spawn enemies inside walls/inside portals.
Fixed an issue where Ace's attacks were getting blocked by things that really shouldn't block them.
Fixed an exceedingly rare bug where the game would go through one frame with a negative timestep, causing crazy screen shake, an erroneous level clear message, a minute or so of being totally frozen, and just generally screwing everything up.


Thanks for reading!

Added the level choice system. At the end of every level, the player will be presented with three portals instead of one, each with a specific boss and level theme.  This gives the player some power to select his path through the game's levels according to what powers he already has and which bosses he wants to take out early or save for later. As the player closes in on level 8, the choices will narrow down (levels 1-5 allow 3 choices, level 6 allows 2, and level 7 has one portal "choice" at the end.)
Much of the control and keybind system has been rewritten. Each player may now choose his own control scheme. 20XX will now detect up to 4 DirectInput devices (up from 2). Players can also now choose which input device to use from the Change Controls menu (which now has a separate menu for P1 and P2). (We've also swapped keybind filenames -- we're now saving "20xxv70alpha.key" to your My Documents folder. You can safely delete eridu.key.)
If your controller doesn't immediately work, you're probably set to the keyboard. Change it in the Change Controls menu!


SMALL CHANGES:

Reverted Ace's 20% damage nerf from a few patches ago. (Relative to last patch, Ace now deals 25% more damage.)
Ace now begins the game with 10 HP (up from 8).
Turret Boss's whirl attack now spins less quickly.
Shield Drones (Alpha version only) will now drop their shield after counterattacking twice.
Reduced the Twins' health by 20%.
Rebalanced Power Boost, and the items that grant it, as follows:

Each point of Power Boost is back to granting 20% damage per point. 
If the player has negative Power Boost (for example, if your first pickup is XCALBER), the penalty per point is 10% (instead of 20% -- last patch, the penalty was a full 30%).
A-Matic now grants 2 Power Boost (up from 1).
In addition to its other effect, Blood Magic now grants 1 Power Boost.
In addition to its other effect, Enerscoop Alpha now grants 1 Power Boost.

In addition to its other effect, Healthfinder 8000 now grants 1 Max HP.
Panther enemies no longer have a weird semi-invulnerability before revealing themselves.
Shield Drone (Frostor) HP reduced by 30%.
Penguin (Frostor) HP reduced by 20%.
Creeper (Frostor) HP reduced by 40%.
Cannon (Skytemple) HP reduced by 15%.
Maceguy (Skytemple) HP reduced by 30%.
Boltfly (Skytemple) HP reduced by 25%.
These are not the big Skytemple/Frostor changes we're working on-- just temporary fixes, since the work on these levels is a little further down our pipeline.


BUG FIXES:

The Twins' Flameshield projectiles had larger hitboxes than their graphic. This has been fixed.
Fixed an issue where Svalinn Gamma (Frostor shield boss) would spawn enemies inside walls/inside portals.
Fixed an issue where Ace's attacks were getting blocked by things that really shouldn't block them.
Fixed an exceedingly rare bug where the game would go through one frame with a negative timestep, causing crazy screen shake, an erroneous level clear message, a minute or so of being totally frozen, and just generally screwing everything up.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.69b Patch Notes - April 29, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! It's super mechanics tweak day. Enjoy!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in alpha. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware! Note: nothing along these lines is happening this patch. 

TL;DR for today's patch: Lots and lots of tweaks and bugfixes. UI no longer sucks when not playing at 1080p. Dash/walljump control mechanic changes. Tweaks to boss invuln (and a fix for co-op). Enemy AI changes. Spawning enemies now indicate where they're coming in before spawning.

For the next patch or two: Boss work, Power work/finalization, more level variability, proper speedrunning mode.

On the horizon (extremely subject to change): online play, safehouse rework, more Leaderboard changes.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Bosses in co-op now have separate invulnerability timers for each player. (We're not currently doing a great job of communicating this.)
Boss invulnerability timer experimentation: timer reduced to 0.5s. This should make not charging your weapon more viable and make multi-hit powers more useful without making them OP, without changing the power of charging up.
Non-piercing attacks no longer travel through invulnerable bosses. Piercing attacks still do, though.
Dashing along the ground no longer suspends gravity. This also fixes a few weird bugs involving dashing on slopes, and dashing into stuff and flying off at weird angles. Air dashing is not affected by this change.
Big fix: Lots of the UI is now less garbage when viewed at non-widescreen (especially non-1080p) resolutions.
Most enemies no longer attack without line of sight.
On the other side of that coin, Ace can no longer damage enemies through walls.

LOS is currently being calculated from player-center to enemy-center -- if this proves too restrictive, we have ways to ease it.



SMALL CHANGES:

Each point of Attack or Power Boost now increases their respective damage type by 30% (up from 20%).
Tweaked wall jumping controls a bit to prevent an irritating control issue involving wall jumping near ceilings that resulted in the player getting "stuck" mashing his head against the ceiling when trying to clear a wall.
A run timer is now displayed in the bottom left corner during gameplay. It can be turned on or off in the Options menu. It doesn't count up while the game is paused or while it's loading.
Several enemies no longer begin their attack animations if the player is on the other side of a wall.
Heavy changes to the drop pre-roll system that should prevent players from seeing multiples of an item before having seen them all at least once. (Missed boxes and unpurchased shop items count toward "having seen them".)
In co-op play, the camera now zooms out more when the players are vertically distant, so it's easier to see what's above/below the players.
The Iron Vanguard (Gorilla Twins) now ping where they're going to teleport to a moment before it happens.
The Iron Vanguard now uses its Flameshield power.
Kur, the Gatekeeper now uses his Quintlaser power.
All enemies summoned by bosses now phase in in grayscale for a moment before materializing.
Soul Foes are now shaded very differently to stand out from their normal counterparts.
Soul Foes are now a bit tankier late in the game. (Shouldn't affect the early levels much.)
Nina's multi-hit weapons now do a little more damage to bosses. (Star Beam excluded.)


BUG FIXES:

Fixed an issue where finishing a level within three seconds of failing the Bonus Timer would print "BONUS ACHIEVED!" even though it was not achieved.
Fixed a bunch of tile errors.
Fixed a bunch of dash-related bugs (see above).
Fixed some busted tooltips.
Fixed an issue causing Nuts and Soul Nuts to ignore the sound controls.
Fixed a bug causing Ace's Rippling Axe to be mostly useless.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.68b Patch Notes - April 15, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! It's Boss and Power Patch Day (#1). Prepare yourself!

Disclaimer: 20XX is in alpha. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware! 

As of today's patch, we'll be wiping the long-term Speedrun and High Score boards, as well as your 20XX save data. Congrats to Saeryf for somehow breaking of our Score leaderboard (9,881 nuts.. on level 3?) and to rob_demir for the fastest completion (886 seconds).

TL;DR for today's patch: Boss mechanics overhauls! Power overhauls! Tons of Flamelab art!

For the next patch or two: Eridu rework, more level variability, more boss work, proper speedrunning mode.

On the horizon (extremely subject to change): online play, safehouse rework, more Leaderboard changes.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Agnisort/Flamelab art has received a massive update, and is much closer to how it'll finally look!
In general, boss fights will now be longer/force the player to actually learn the mechanics, because...
Bosses now have invulnerability timers (1 second).
Bosses can now be weak to certain Powers -- discover them all!
Bosses now drop a specific Power (instead of a random one).
Rollster B now uses its Boomerang Blade in combat (and drops it after his death).
Turret Boss now uses and drops Vera.
Penguin Boss now uses and drops Splinterfrost.
Lotus now uses Mortar as part of its attack rotation.
Eternal Star (bat boss) moved to Eridu. In a future patch, Eridu will not be a special level; instead, the game will have a Wily-style level 9 to end the run.
Destroyer of Diamonds (exploder boss) is on vacation.
Powers no longer need to be unlocked via Soul Nuts. (In this patch, only the Passives are unlocked via Soul Nuts. Skulls may be added to the Soul Nut Unlock list soon, or we might make them achievement-based.)
The bosses that don't clearly use the weapons they drop currently will do so next patch (April 29 2015).
[strike]Weapon charge time increased to 2 seconds (up from 1). Our thinking: Charging is supposed to be something you do in between combats, or very purposefully for reach/cleave (instead of all the time, which 1 second allows for). Items will be available soon that reduce charge time.[/strike] We've reverted this change pending more testing. Charge attacks still take one second.



SMALL CHANGES:

Starting Energy increased to 12 (up from 8). Passives that grant Energy now grant more. Energy pickups now restore 2 and 5 for small and large pickups, respectively (up from 1 and 3).
Splinterfrost reworked to be more attractive. The splinters now fire off in front of the weapon.
Boomerang Blade is now more metal. It can be thrown in 8 directions, based on the direction the player's pressing.
Flameshield has been reworked. It's no longer a toggled power; instead, on use, it spawns four flames that either deal damage to the first enemy hit, or block the first enemy bullet they come in contact with.
Blastjump has been replaced with Nova, found after beating Svalinn Gamma (shield drone boss). Nova is a powerful AOE attack that also destroys enemy projectiles on use.
Ace's base weapon damage has been reduced by 20%.
Dashing on slippery surfaces is now much more responsive. (Maybe too responsive. We'll see.)
The Bonus Timer now stops once you've beaten the boss. Additionally, it now does a better job of explaining itself. (More coming on this.)
Nutrageous and Nut Farm (passive items) removed. Nutrageous was anti-fun, and Nut Farm was crazily overpowered.
Arctech's Shield Drones can now only retaliate once every quarter second (instead of once every frame), mostly for performance reasons.
Health Nut and Charged Nuts now restore the appropriate resource 20% of the time (down from 100%). The chance stacks additively with other Health/Charged Nut pickups, and caps at 100%. Their Shop values have been decreased to account for the nerf.
XCALBER nerfed. MaxHP down to 2 (from 3). Attack boost down to 1 (from 2).
TANK! nerfed. Attack boost down to 1 (from 2). Power boost removed. 
Vera's damage increased by 50%. Vera's energy cost increased by 100%. Vera has a special ability: it does not trigger boss invulnerability timers. (This might be super OP. We'll see!)
Co-op camera zoom max speed increased by 900%.
Added some better signaling in the Safehouse about purchases unlocking items, instead of permanently granting them.
Transmute removed. (We're getting rid of Powers that don't have combat uses, but this ability might come back another way. Maybe!)
Datalore is on hiatus while we do it correctly.
Enemy Nut droprate reduced by 50%.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed an issue causing normal playthroughs to register on the Hardcore leaderboard, using up a player's try for the day.
Fixed an issue causing the tutorial's boss room platforms to fail to appear.
Fixed an issue causing every Speedrun leaderboard entry to say the player used Ace, even if he didn't.
Fixed a bug causing some funky Flameshield interactions.
Hopefully fixed a bug causing the game to display the wrong input in the tutorial. (This probably needs more work.)


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.67b Patch Notes - April 1, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! It's Leaderboard Patch Day. Do you have what it takes to be the very best?

Disclaimer: 20XX is in alpha. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements, and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware! We anticipate the need to do this for the first time in the April 15, 2015 patch. (We thought we'd do it today, April 1, but pushed it back two weeks.)

TL;DR for today's patch: Leaderboard support! Daily seeded challenges! Daily hardcore challenges! Probably bugs involving all three!!

For the next patch or two: Eridu rework, more level variability, moving Skulls into the unlock system, more boss work, proper speedrunning mode, lots more art!

On the horizon (extremely subject to change): online play, safehouse rework, more Leaderboard changes.

ALSO: We've submitted our first price increase to Valve. When approved, 20XX's price will increase to $9.99 USD.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Added the Daily Challenge mode. Each day (resets at midnight PST) the Daily Challenge offers players a unique set of levels that's the same for everyone who plays it that day. (It's a seeded run.) You only get one attempt at each Daily Challenge! If you die or quit, you'll have to wait until tomorrow's Daily Challenge to try again. In Daily Challenges, Soul Foes drop 5 nuts instead of Soul Nuts.
Added the Daily Hardcore mode. It's similar to the Daily Challenge, but each Daily Hardcore comes with 3 randomly chosen Skulls activated. It's also a once-per-day deal, and the levels generated are the same for all players.
20XX now has Leaderboard support! For now, 20XX tracks your highest nutscore and fastest game completion time, as well as high nutscores for the Daily Challenge and Daily Hardcore modes. (Next patch, we'll have fastest run leaderboards for the Dailies, too.) Access the Leaderboards from the Title Screen. (Art for the Leaderboards option WIP.)
Reorganized the Safehouse to accomodate the new Challenge portals. (This isn't our official Safehouse rework.)


SMALL CHANGES:

Players now start with 8 energy by default (up from 6).
Gave Agnisort's moving platforms some better feel. (There'll be proper tracks for them soon, too!)
Silver Crates have been nerfed substantially.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed an issue where Skulls that should prevent certain item spawns were failing to do so.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.66b Patch Notes - March 18, 2015
notes.content:
Hello! Today's patch notes will include some of the ones from last patch, since we typed that post in an awful pre-PAX hurry.

Disclaimer: 20XX is in alpha. As we develop the game, we may make changes that require us to invalidate or wipe your 20XX save files, Steam Leaderboard info/achievements (these aren't in game yet!), and other save-y stuff like that. Be aware! We anticipate the need to do this for the first time in the April 1, 2015 patch.

TL;DR for today's patch: Lots of fixes and post-PAX related changes. Big Eridu bandaid nerfs. (We'll be changing Eridu a lot in the next few patches, but level 4 Eridu was just too punishing.) New art!

We're also delighted to announce that Clemens Scott (of Broken Rules, a fantastic game studio in Vienna, Austria) will be joining the 20XX crew as Art Director to help us take our visuals to the next level. Be prepared for lots and lots of beautiful changes in the weeks and months to come.

For the next patch or two: Eridu rework, more level variability, moving Skulls into the unlock system, more boss work, proper speedrun mode.

On the horizon (extremely subject to change): online play, safehouse rework, daily challenges (seeded runs with a set number of skulls on, later with Steam Leaderboard integration.

ALSO: As of next patch (4/1), we'll be bumping our Early Access price up to $9.99. The price will continue to rise as we get closer to launch.)

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Eridu-4 is now less insanely difficult. Eridu-8 is still super hard, but it's the end of the game. It should be! Most attacks in E-4 do 1 damage (down from 2). Spikes/falling deal 1 damage in E-4 (down from 2). Enemy density in E-4 halved. (This is not our Big Eridu Change. It is just a bandaid fix.)
Added Armor Capsules (placeholder art). Armor capsules artificially extend your Health bar, and take damage instead of Health. (Any damage you take will reduce your Armor first -- even if you don't have enough to absorb the full hit!)
Ace's 3-hit Saber combo returns! Each slash has a unique graphic and the third hit deals extra damage.
Kur, the Gatekeeper now awaits would-be saviors in Eridu-4 (instead of placeholder Enlil).
Changed the blending style for many of our particles and projectiles. Behold the glowing glory! (We think this counts as a big change.)


SMALL CHANGES:

Added lots of new pickup effects.
Resurrection is now a little more forgiving in co-op. Players performing resurrections can't be reduced below 3 HP, and resurrecting players come back with at least 3 HP.
Soul Nut pickups now randomly award 1-5 Soul Nuts instead of 3.
Reduced the base chance that "small" enemies drop small nuts by 50% (from 20% to 10%). Their chance to drop large nuts (2%) remains unchanged. (Our first economy rework resulted in a nut glut.)
The camera in the boss room is now fixed.
New art for the Boomerang Blade (and it goes a little further than it used to.)


BUG FIXES:

Fixed some collision spots and bad enemy placements.
Fixed some slope dashing errors. (This one's been a work in progress. Here's hoping!)


Thanks for reading!

ALSO: As of next patch (4/1), we'll be bumping our Early Access price up to $9.99. The price will continue to rise as we get closer to launch.)

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Eridu-4 is now less insanely difficult. Eridu-8 is still super hard, but it's the end of the game. It should be! Most attacks in E-4 do 1 damage (down from 2). Spikes/falling deal 1 damage in E-4 (down from 2). Enemy density in E-4 halved. (This is not our Big Eridu Change. It is just a bandaid fix.)
Added Armor Capsules (placeholder art). Armor capsules artificially extend your Health bar, and take damage instead of Health. (Any damage you take will reduce your Armor first -- even if you don't have enough to absorb the full hit!)
Ace's 3-hit Saber combo returns! Each slash has a unique graphic and the third hit deals extra damage.
Kur, the Gatekeeper now awaits would-be saviors in Eridu-4 (instead of placeholder Enlil).
Changed the blending style for many of our particles and projectiles. Behold the glowing glory! (We think this counts as a big change.)


SMALL CHANGES:

Added lots of new pickup effects.
Resurrection is now a little more forgiving in co-op. Players performing resurrections can't be reduced below 3 HP, and resurrecting players come back with at least 3 HP.
Soul Nut pickups now randomly award 1-5 Soul Nuts instead of 3.
Reduced the base chance that "small" enemies drop small nuts by 50% (from 20% to 10%). Their chance to drop large nuts (2%) remains unchanged. (Our first economy rework resulted in a nut glut.)
The camera in the boss room is now fixed.
New art for the Boomerang Blade (and it goes a little further than it used to.)


BUG FIXES:

Fixed some collision spots and bad enemy placements.
Fixed some slope dashing errors. (This one's been a work in progress. Here's hoping!)


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.64b Patch Notes -- February 18th, 2015
notes.content:
Evening!

TL;DR for today's patch: New item unlock and difficulty systems! Acquire Soul Nuts in game to unlock awesome stuff that can then be found in-game. Activate Skulls to make your journeys into the Network that much more harrowing.

(Our Skulls art is placeholder, and our character select capsule is work in progress.)

For next time: Lots of stuff to clean up before we go to PAX East!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes.

--

BIG CHANGES:

NEW DIFFICULTY SYSTEM: Carry the weight of your forebears. Activate Skulls before you play that radically modify the game when activated! The currently implemented Skulls are:

Marathon: All levels are longer.
Lightning: The game runs at 150% speed.
Famine: No health items drop.
Bankrupt: No nuts drop. No stores or vending machines.
Rock: Spikes and pits deal 99999 damage (instant death).
Purist: No dash, speed, or jump upgrades spawn. (Aerial Stabilizer/Airdash still spawns.)
Toxin: The bonus timer is replaced by the Toxin timer. When it runs out, you'll take one damage every five seconds until the level is complete or you are complete.
Swarm: More enemies spawn.
Furor: Enemies have haste. (Move/attackspeed +50%)
Undying: Enemies have more health.
Wrath: Enemies deal double damage.
Final Destination: No items. Fox only. (That last part is a joke.)

Skulls can be toggled on and off at the Safehouse (where you once again start the game).
Most Skulls are unlocked now, but will need to be unlocked by the player later in development. The art for the Skulls is placeholder.
NEW UNLOCK SYSTEM: Stand on the shoulders of your past selves. Many great powers lie locked in the recesses of your technology; unlock them using glorious Soul Nuts, acquired from Soul Foes during play.

Blue-glowing enemies within levels are Soul Foes - they have increased health and are more aggressive. 
Defeating them will award some Soul Nuts, which can be spent after your inevitable demise at the Safehouse. 
The Shopkeep in the Safehouse takes Soul Nuts for his items; once purchased in the Safehouse, you can find the items in game.
When you leave the Safehouse, your Soul Nuts are lost.

A new foe, the forgotten Forest Spirit, enters the fray. (For now, it shows up sometimes in Vaculab.)
A new power, Splinterfrost, is now available (once unlocked for 5 soul nuts).
You should no longer see enemies "reset" while you're anywhere near them. (Previously, enemies that wandered too far from their home would just really want to go home. We've decreased their homesickness parameter by 100%.)
Some changes have been made to the physics engine to perform better under low frame rates.



SMALL CHANGES:

The Pickup Display (the thing that pops up at the bottom of the screen) now appears when you are touching the item, instead of only appearing once picked up.
Ace's Plasma Blender charges faster (0.5 seconds) and his Rippling Axe charges more slowly (4 seconds, and it still might be OP).
In-game menus now loop. (You can scroll from the bottom to the top by pressing down, etc.)
Ace's Sharp Sharp Spear now deals 20% less damage.
Added lots of new graphical effects for various items.
Blood Magic has been redesigned. It now gives a chance to grant health when killing an enemy with a Power.
Shadespur has been slightly reworked. It now inherits the player's velocity when you fire it (instead of being perfectly still).
The Gold Stud has been redesigned. On using a Power, it now grants a 30% chance to refund the energy spent on that Power. (Over time, this is very similar to "powers cost 30% less", but it feels better.)
Enemies that remain inactive until the player gets within a certain distance of them also now activate upon taking damage.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a hideous Eridu you-instantly-die bug.
Fixed some collision issues with the new invisible-wall-less levels.
Fixed a bug preventing some passive items from appearing in Gold Chests.
Fixed a bug preventing the Steam Overlay from activating. (If you still have this problem, tell us!)
Finally figured out the cause of a Frostor visual glitch (where one of the light-up blocks draws really weirdly across the screen). If you see it, take a screenshot and tell us!
Improved some resolution-detection code. If you previously couldn't change resolution, you probably can now!



Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.63b Patch Notes -- February 4, 2015
notes.content:
Hello!

TL;DR for today's patch: Some big quality of life/polish changes that have been requested by the community.

For next time: bringing back the unlocks/progression system, as well as our campaign/endless mode splits! (And hopefully some other fun features.)

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes.

--

BIG CHANGES:

Picking stuff up -- passives, powers, new primaries, etc -- is now done via the Activate Things button. This also applies to vending machines. No more awkward primary fire/standing on the item to get it. (This button is B by default on a 360 controller, and A by default on a keyboard.) All stuff the Activate Things button interacts with will display a prompt telling you what button to push. The prompt will change if you remap the key.)
NO MORE INVISIBLE WALLS! Level architectures have been redesigned such that invisible walls are no longer necessary. Let us know if you see otherwise!
Dash jumping handles a bit differently: once you're airborne, you'll stop moving horizontally if you let go of the key for the direction you're moving in (left/right stick/dpad, or the arrow keys by default). This makes dash jumping a bit easier to control, and feels more intuitive to players.


SMALL CHANGES:

Modified penguin enemy behavior to be more interesting.
Angel Nineteen (Arctech penguin boss) is now more threatening.
New Ace and Nina heads. Less cartoony. Tell us what you think!
More graphical tweaks.
Pickups from chests and enemies now have their horizontal velocities when they pop out reduced by 50%. Hopefully fewer items fall into the abyss, but, you know, that's sort of on you, isn't it?


BUG FIXES:

Fixed an issue where you could jump between rooms into "blank space" in the level, and the game would think you've fallen and need to be ported back to safety. (You can still do this -- the game just defines what counts as a fall a bit differently now.)
Fixed a long-standing bug where sometimes one player wall-jumping would impact the other player's movement in co-op.
Fixed some bugs re: last patch's co-op changes.
Fixed a bug where sometimes you'd dash on a fall-through platform and not be able to jump.
Fixed a bug where the Lotus boss would still damage the player after dying.
Fixed a bug (hopefully) where bees will use their sting-a-splode attack and fail to a-splode. Let us know if you see bees failing to a-splode.


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.62b Patch Notes -- January 21, 2015
notes.content:
Hey guys! This is our pre-MAGFest update -- we'll be there this weekend (at National Harbor in Maryland) instead of PAX South, so if you're there, come check us out in the MIVS area!

TL;DR for today's patch: lots of co-op tweaks and changes to improve quality and smoothness. Also a bunch of boss tweaks, including some redesigns!

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes. Thanks again!

--

BIG CHANGES:

Frostor's flash-freeze mechanic has been changed. Now, instead of heat zones, these areas feature a targeting reticule that closes in on the player over a few seconds, then attacks. The reticule is reset by standing in a green Shield Zone. This gives players much more control over how they traverse these rooms.
Vaculab's Gorilla boss has been redesigned.
Vaculab has a new Lotus boss! 
Dragonboss (Herald of Flame) removed -- he'll be back elsewhere with a vengeance.
Rolly boss (Rollster Beta) now has a hardmode form if you encounter him on your second visit to Flamelab. (All bosses will have these pretty soon.)
In Co-op, passive upgrades now apply to the team, instead of having to fight over them. This is to avoid the situation where Player 1 gets a movespeed boost and a double jump, and Player 2 does not. (It sucks having to wait for your teammates because of uneven items.)
In Co-op, players now spawn a resurrection shrine a few rooms up when they die. You can't res them where they die anymore. (It was awkward gameplay, and sometimes really frustrating -- especially when a player died on a spike.) It still costs half your health!
In Co-op, end-of-level red crates now drop one weapon for each player. Each player can only take one, though! No hogging.
Some bosses now have a tiny bit of speech.


SMALL CHANGES:

Lots and lots and lots of tile/level changes. Frostor is no longer terribly difficult the first time you encounter it. (Eridu still is, but we'll fix that later.)
Eternal Star (Agnisort Bat Boss) has been given a facelift, and behaves slightly differently.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a bug where Ace could only start a weapon charge-up while on the ground.
Fixed some instances of a goofy Arctech graphical glitch, but probably not all of them :(
Fixed a co-op bug where bosses would sit at 1hp if player 2 entered the arena alone.
Other small stuff.


Thanks for reading! Keep the feedback coming -- it really keeps us going! Come see us at MAGFest this weekend (Jan 23-26) at National Harbor in Maryland!

notes.title: 20XX 0.61b Patch Notes -- Jan 7, 2015
notes.content:
20XX moves forward today with a smaller-than-normal patch. (We're humans who like to spend the holidays with our families and friends, too.)

Today's patch brings a few big things -- much clearer indications of what you're picking up and the damage you're dealing in the form of indicator numbers and messages, another beta enemy, and an additional step toward our economy overhaul.

Coming up next (not in today's patch): Better difficulty scaling in terms of level generation, more level variance, boss overhauls, and the return of our ingame progression system.

As always, let us know if anything's busted or if we missed some changes. Thanks again!

--

BIG CHANGES:

All store items now have cost ranges based on their value (instead of always costing 15). In every case, this is a central value +/- 20%. (This is one of the economic changes we're making in 20XX -- more to come soon!)
Lots of in-game indicator text, including:

Damage numbers on enemy hit (will be controllable via options next patch)
Damage taken when the player is hit
Notifications when picking up health, energy, and nuts
Warnings when the player tries to do something he can't (pressing the Power key without a Power, or without enough energy, or trying to buy an item he can't afford)
Notifications when spending nuts



SMALL CHANGES:

Players are now differently colored if they're the same character in co-op play.
Players now have infinite HP/Energy in the tutorial, and the HP/Energy bars no longer display during it.
All items that give +MaxHP or +MaxEnergy should now give you full new bars, not empty ones. (If you see any that don't seem to obey this rule, tell us!)
Another beta-type enemy in the form of the Penguin.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed an issue with Ace's charge where he'd sometimes effectively get two charged attacks in a row.
Fixed a bug where dashing on magnetic ceilings would cause insane results.
Fixed bugs causing bats to not move horizontally and lotuses to freak out. (May have also fixed a bee bug, but we're not 100% on this one.)


Thanks for reading!

notes.title: 20XX 0.60b Patch Notes -- Dec 24, 2014
notes.content:
20XX releases its Christmas Eve patch today! (It's the Christmas Eve patch because it's being released on Christmas Eve. 20XX contains no merry or jubilant content.)

TL;DR: Lots of new enemy variations, sweet new Powers, some balance changes, greater nut yield, and more!

BIG CHANGES:

Many enemies now come in Alpha and Beta forms. For the most part, Alpha forms are the ones you're used to seeing, and behave similarly. Beta forms have new art and new attack styles, and show up more as you progress through the game. More Beta forms will be coming in future updates.
Exceptions to the "alpha" behavior rule: 
	Alpha Bees dive and explode, but only Beta Bees release fireballs.
	Alpha Turrets are no longer protected before the player gets close. Beta Turrets maintain this functionality with a much more obvious shield effect.

As the first step of an economy overhaul, enemies now drop more nuts. 
	Small enemies drop an average of 0.3 nuts, up from 0.08. 
	Big enemies drop an average of 0.6 nuts, up from 0.16.

Four new powers have been added to 20XX, and can be found in red crates like the others.

	The Blastjump creates a localized explosion around your feet, dealing damage to nearby enemies and propelling you upward.
	The Flameshield is the first of a new type of Power: the Toggled Power. When activated, the Flameshield surrounds you with vicious flames until you either turn it off (by pressing the Power button again) or run out of energy.
	The Transposer is a utility Power -- when activated, it fires a tiny projectile that, if it connects with an enemy, will swap your position with that of your victim. It works on bosses! (For now. We're probably going to nerf it.)
	The Quint Laser's bullet is enormous. There is no escaping it.

Ace can now charge his weapon!
The Lotus, an old enemy from the Spacejungle, has been re-added to the game.

	
SMALL CHANGES:

Lots of new art for various pickups.
"Secondary weapons" are now "Powers." Better name. References to secondary weapons have been changed across the board (so if you see any, let us know).
The Bronze, Silver, and Platinum Studs have been removed. (They clogged up the passive item pool without providing much fun.)
Characters now dash up and down slopes a little more smoothly. We're still iterating on this.
Clock now costs 2 energy (down from 5).
Transmute now costs 2 energy (down from 3).
Snake health reduced by 30%.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a Wave Beam bug where it'd sometimes do an outrageous amount of damage when charged up.
Other small fixes that I can't remember right this moment and will not take the time to look up because it's Christmas Eve and it's time for Family Stuff On Christmas Eve now.

Thanks for reading -- happy holidays!

The Bronze, Silver, and Platinum Studs have been removed. (They clogged up the passive item pool without providing much fun.)
Characters now dash up and down slopes a little more smoothly. We're still iterating on this.
Clock now costs 2 energy (down from 5).
Transmute now costs 2 energy (down from 3).
Snake health reduced by 30%.


BUG FIXES:

Fixed a Wave Beam bug where it'd sometimes do an outrageous amount of damage when charged up.
Other small fixes that I can't remember right this moment and will not take the time to look up because it's Christmas Eve and it's time for Family Stuff On Christmas Eve now.

Thanks for reading -- happy holidays!

notes.title: 20XX Dec 10 2014 Patch Notes
notes.content:
20XX's first post-Early Access bi-weekly update is here! It should be live a few minutes after this post goes up.

TL;DR version: we added powerful new primary weapons for Nina and Ace to equip during play, and began developing out our DATALORE system (for telling our story). Levels 1 and 2 are a little easier than before. We also made a billion other changes, but they're less big.

See the full notes below!

--

BIG CHANGES:

Ace and Nina can now find new primary weapons on their journey. These weapons are found in diamond (blue) chests, which sometimes take the place of gold chests. Wield the Rippling Axe, the Forkalator, and many more weapons to help you slay your foes. Discover them all! (Eventually, you'll have to unlock them, but for now, enjoy!)
The first set of DATALORE is in-game! Find Nina's diaries in each level. (Ace's and some other important logs are not in yet!)
The first stage of a run is always a bit shorter, and the enemies/boss are easier.
Frostor can no longer be found as the first stage of a run.
In campaign, Eridu is now always level 6 (up from 4).


SMALL CHANGES:


Vending machines at the end of a level now have new art, and display the relevant keys for interacting with them. (The same will be done for co-op resurrection and picking up weapons/passives in a later update.)
The Mortar subweapon has been redesigned, and now has new art.
Vera (subweapon) has been given a rework -- better art pending.
Added the Diamond Crate (better art pending), containing new powerful primary weapons.
Made several effects a little flashier.
Eridu's Mechannon blasts no longer bounce. (They now explode on contact.)
Made a few tweaks to the way text is displayed, especially at lower resolutions.
Enlil, final boss placeholder supreme, no longer annihilates himself shortly after the battle begins.


Lots and lots of little fixes and tweaks, as always. Let us know if you see changes that aren't listed here!

Thanks for reading and playing! We've gotten a ton of great feedback in the past few weeks that should find its way into our upcoming updates. Keep it coming!

Cheers
Chris
